(Surat al-Nahl)
Meccan, except for the last three verses, which are Medinan.
Its verses number 128. It was revealed after Surat al-Kahf.
Al-Asamm related from some scholars that the whole surah is Medinan. Others said that from its beginning up to His words ﴿Be, and it is﴾ it is Medinan, and what comes after that is Meccan. Qatadah held the reverse.
Know that this surah is called Surat al-Ni'am (the Surah of Blessings). It has 128 verses and is Meccan.

[In the Name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful]

﴿The command of God has come, so do not seek to hasten it. Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they associate with Him.﴾ ﴿He sends down the angels with the Spirit by His command, upon whom He wills of His servants, [saying]: "Warn that there is no deity except Me, so fear Me."﴾

[In the Name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful]

﴿The command of God has come, so do not seek to hasten it. Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they associate with Him.﴾ ﴿He sends down the angels with the Spirit by His command, upon whom He wills of His servants, [saying]: "Warn that there is no deity except Me, so fear Me."﴾

There are several issues concerning this verse.

The first issue: Know that understanding the interpretation of this verse depends on three questions.

The first question: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) would warn them sometimes of the punishment of this world, namely killing and their subjugation, as happened on the day of Badr, and sometimes of the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, which occurs at the establishment of the Hour. When the people did not witness any of that, they used it as an argument to deny him, and they demanded that he bring that punishment, saying to him: "Bring it to us." It is narrated that when God's words were revealed, ﴿The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has been split﴾ [al-Qamar 54:1], the disbelievers said among themselves: "This man claims that the Resurrection has come near, so refrain from some of your deeds until we see what will happen." When it was delayed, they said: "We see nothing of what you threaten us with." Then God revealed: ﴿The reckoning of the people has drawn near﴾ [al-Anbiya' 21:1], so they became fearful and waited for its day. When the days stretched on, they said: "O Muhammad, we see nothing of what you threaten us with." Then God revealed: ﴿The command of God has come﴾. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) jumped up, and the people raised their heads, and then God revealed: ﴿So do not seek to hasten it.﴾

[Page 174]

﴿...seek to hasten it.﴾ The summary is that when he (peace be upon him) repeatedly threatened them with the punishment of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter, and they saw nothing, they accused him of lying.

God answered this doubt with His words: ﴿The command of God has come, so do not seek to hasten it.﴾ In explaining this answer there are two views.

The first view: Although that punishment had not yet come, it was certain to occur. When something is in this state and this condition, it is common speech to say that it has already come and has occurred, treating what must occur as though it had already occurred. One says to someone who asked for relief and whose relief is near: "Relief has come to you, so do not despair."

The second view: The command of God and His judgment concerning it has already come, taken place, and occurred. As for what was judged, it has not yet occurred, because God decreed its occurrence at a specific time, and before that time arrives it does not come into existence. The meaning is as if it were said: The command of God and His judgment to send down the punishment has been established and has existed from eternity to eternity. So our saying "The command of God has come" is correct. However, what was judged and commanded has not yet taken place, because God specified its occurrence for a fixed time. So do not seek to hasten it, and do not demand its occurrence before that time comes.

The second question: The disbelievers said: Suppose we accept from you, O Muhammad, the truth of what you say, that God has decreed to send down punishment upon us, either in this world or in the Hereafter. Still, we worship these idols, for they are our intercessors with God, and they will intercede for us with Him, so we shall be spared this decreed punishment through the intercession of these idols.

God answered this doubt with His words: ﴿Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they associate with Him.﴾ He thereby declared Himself free from having partners, rivals, and equals, and from any spirit or body having the right to intercede with Him except by His permission. The word (ma) in His words ﴿what they associate with Him﴾ may be a verbal noun (maṣdariyyah), so the meaning is "exalted is He above their association," or it may mean "that which" (alladhi), so the meaning is "exalted is He above these idols which they have made partners with God, because they are lifeless, base objects, so what relation do they have to Him, let alone to be judged as partners of the Governor of the earth and the heavens."

The third question: Suppose God has decreed for some of His servants happiness and for others hardship. But how can you know these secrets which no one knows except God? And how have you come to know the secrets of God and His judgments in His dominion and His kingdom?

God answered this with His words: ﴿He sends down the angels with the Spirit by His command, upon whom He wills of His servants, [saying]: "Warn that there is no deity except Me, so fear Me."﴾ The explanation of this answer is that God sends down the angels upon whomever He wills of His servants, and commands that servant to convey to all creation that the God of the worlds is One, who has obligated them to know His oneness and to worship Him, and who has made clear that if they do this they will succeed in the good of this world and the Hereafter, and if they rebel they will fall into the evil of this world and the Hereafter. In this way he is specially given these knowledges above all other creatures. And it has become clear through this arrangement that we have summarized that these verses are organized in the best manner. And God knows best. In the verse there are several issues:

The first issue: Nafi', 'Asim, Hamzah, and al-Kisa'i read (yunazzilu) with a ya' and with kasrah on the zay and shaddah, and al-Malaikata in the accusative. Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr read (yunzilu) with a damma on the ya' and kasrah on the zay and without shaddah. The first is from the form (tafa'ul) and the second from the form (if'al), and both are two dialects.

The second issue: It is narrated from 'Ata' from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: By "the angels" he means Jibril alone. Al-Wahidi said: Calling one by the name of the plural is permissible when that one is a leader and chief, as in God's words: ﴿Indeed, We sent Nuh to his people﴾ [Nuh 71:1], and ﴿Indeed, We sent it down﴾ [al-Qadr 97:1], and ﴿Indeed, We have sent down the Reminder﴾ [al-Hijr 15:9]. And in reference to people, as in: ﴿those to whom the people said﴾ [Al 'Imran 3:173]. There is another view concerning this, which will be explained after this. As for His words ﴿with the Spirit by His command﴾, there are two views:

The first view: The Spirit here means the revelation, which is the speech of God. A similar verse is His words: ﴿And thus We have revealed to you a Spirit of Our command﴾ [al-Shura 42:52], and His words: ﴿He sends down the Spirit by His command upon whom He wills of His servants﴾ [Ghafir 40:15]. The people of verification said: The body is dead, dense, and dark. When the spirit is joined to it, it becomes living, subtle, and luminous, so the traces of light appear in the five senses. Then the spirit is also dark and ignorant, and when the intellect is joined to it, it becomes radiant and luminous, as God said: ﴿And God brought you out from the wombs of your mothers, knowing nothing, and He made for you hearing, sight, and hearts﴾ [al-Nahl 16:78]. Then the intellect too is not complete in luminosity, purity, and radiance until it is perfected by knowledge of the essence of God, His attributes and actions, and knowledge of the states of the world of spirits and bodies, and the world of this life and the Hereafter. These noble divine knowledges are not perfected nor purified except by the light of revelation and the Qur'an.

Knowing this, we say: The Qur'an and revelation through it perfect the divine knowledges and the divine unveilings, and through these knowledges the intellect shines, becomes pure, and is perfected, and through the intellect the essence of the spirit is perfected, and through the spirit the state of the body is perfected. At this point it becomes clear that the true original spirit is revelation and the Qur'an, because through it one is freed from the sleep of ignorance and the slumber of heedlessness, and through it one moves from the depths of animality to the heights of angelic nature. Thus it is clear that applying the word "spirit" to revelation is most fitting and harmonious. What strengthens this is that God applied the word "spirit" to Jibril (peace be upon him) in His words: ﴿The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down upon your heart﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 26:193], and to 'Isa (peace be upon him) in His words: ﴿the Spirit of God﴾ [Yusuf 12:87]. This application was fitting because through the existence of both of them life came to the heart, which is guidance and knowledge. Since the name "spirit" was fittingly applied to them for this meaning, it is even more fitting to apply the word "spirit" to revelation and the sending down.

The second view on this verse, which is the view of Abu 'Ubaydah, is that the Spirit here is Jibril (peace be upon him), and the preposition (bi) in His words ﴿with the Spirit﴾ means "with," as in the common expression "So-and-so went out with his clothes," meaning "with his clothes," and "the commander rode with his weapons," meaning "with his weapons." So the meaning is: He sends down the angels with the Spirit, who is Jibril. The first view is closer. The explanation of this view is that God, glory be to Him and exalted, did not send Jibril alone down upon Muhammad (ﷺ). Rather, in most circumstances he descended with groups of angels accompanying Jibril (peace be upon him). Do you not see that on the day of Badr and in many of the battles, groups of angels descended with Jibril (peace be upon him)? And at times the angel of the mountains would descend upon the Messenger of God (ﷺ), at times the angel of the seas, at times Ridwan, and at times others. His words ﴿by His command﴾ mean that this sending down and descent does not occur except by the command of God, the Exalted. A similar verse is His words: ﴿And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord﴾ [Maryam 19:64], and His words: ﴿They do not precede Him in speech, and they act by His command﴾ [al-Anbiya' 21:27], and His words: ﴿and they are fearful of Him﴾ [al-Anbiya' 21:28], and His words: ﴿They fear their Lord above them and do what they are commanded﴾ [al-Nahl 16:50], and His words: ﴿They do not disobey God in what He commands them, and they do what they are commanded﴾ [al-Tahrim 66:6]. All these verses indicate that they do not undertake any action except by the command and permission of God, the Exalted. His words ﴿upon whom He wills of His servants﴾ [Ghafir 40:15] refer to the prophets whom God specially chose for His message. His words ﴿that warn﴾: al-Zajjaj said: "That" (an) is an appositive to "the Spirit," and the meaning is: He sends down the angels, that they may warn, that is, inform the creatures that there is no deity except Me. Warning is informing together with frightening.

* * *

The second issue: In the verse there are several benefits.

The first benefit: The arrival of revelation from God to the prophets happens only through the mediation of the angels. What strengthens this is that God said at the end of Surat al-Baqarah: ﴿The believers each believe in God and His angels and His books and His messengers﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:285]. He began with the mention of God, glory be to Him, then followed it with the mention of the angels, because they are the ones who receive revelation from God directly without an intermediary, and that revelation is the books. Then the angels convey that revelation to the prophets. Therefore the correct order is to begin with the mention of God the Exalted, then the mention of the angels, then the mention of the books, and in the fourth rank the mention of the messengers.

Knowing this, we say: When God reveals to an angel, the angel's knowledge that this revelation is God's revelation is either a necessary knowledge or an inferred knowledge. If it is inferred, how is the path to it? Also, when the angel conveys that revelation to the Messenger, the Messenger's knowledge that he is a truthful angel and not an accursed devil is either necessary or inferred. If it is inferred, how is the path to it? These are narrow stations, and complete knowledge of them is attained only by investigating the reality of the angel, the manner of God's revelation to him, and the manner in which the angel conveys that revelation to the Messenger. As for applying these matters to ordinary words, the matter becomes difficult and the order collapses. This is because the verses of the Qur'an state clearly that this revelation and sending down came from the angels. Or we may say: Suppose the verses of the Qur'an did not indicate this, still the possibility that the matter is so remains established in the immediate judgment of reason.

And when you have understood this, we say: we do not know that Jibril (peace be upon him) is truthful and protected from lying and deception except through the transmitted (samʿiyyah) evidences. The soundness of the transmitted evidences depends on Muhammad (ﷺ) being truthful, and his truthfulness depends on this Qur'an being a miracle from Allah the Exalted, not from an evil devil (shaytan). Knowing that depends on knowing that Jibril is truthful, rightful, free of deception and free of the works of the devil. In that case, circularity (dawr) necessarily follows. So this is a difficult position. However, once we know the reality of prophethood (nubuwwah) and know the reality of revelation (wahy), this doubt disappears entirely. And Allah knows best.

The fourth issue: this verse shows that the spirit referred to in His saying ﴿He sends down the angels with the spirit by His command﴾ is nothing other than His saying ﴿There is no god but I, so fear Me.﴾ This is a true statement, because the levels of human felicity (sa'adat) are four.

The first is the psychic (nafsaniyya) felicities.

The second is the bodily felicities.

The third level is the bodily attributes that are not essential to the body.

The fourth level is the matters that are separate from the body.

As for the first level, which is the psychic perfections, know that the soul (nafs) has two faculties.

The first is its readiness to receive the forms of existing things from the world of the unseen. This faculty is called the theoretical faculty (al-quwwa al-nazariyya), and its felicity lies in attaining knowledge. The most noble and exalted of knowledge is knowing that there is no god but Him, and to this refers His saying ﴿that warn [people] that there is no god but I, so fear Me.﴾

The second faculty of the soul is its readiness to act upon the bodies of this world. This faculty is called the practical faculty (al-quwwa al-'amaliyya), and its felicity lies in performing righteous deeds. The most noble of righteous deeds is the worship of God, the Exalted, and to this refers His saying ﴿so fear Me.﴾ Since the theoretical faculty is more noble than the practical faculty, God, the Exalted, therefore placed the perfections of the theoretical faculty, which is His saying ﴿There is no god but I﴾, before the perfections of the practical faculty, which is His saying ﴿so fear Me.﴾

As for the second level, which is the bodily felicities, these are also of two kinds: bodily health, and the perfections of the animal faculties, that is, the seventeen bodily faculties.

As for the third level, which is the felicities connected with accidental bodily attributes, these too are of two kinds: the felicity of origins and branches, that is, the perfection of the state of parents, and the perfection of the state of children.

As for the fourth level, which is the lowest of the levels, it consists of the felicities that arise from external matters, namely wealth and status.

Thus it is established that the most noble levels of felicity are the psychic states, and these are confined to the perfections of the theoretical and practical faculties. For this reason God mentioned here the highest state of these two faculties, saying ﴿that warn [people] that there is no god but I, so fear Me.﴾

[p. 177]

**The commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on Surah 16, verse 3:**

**His saying, exalted is He:** ﴿He created the heavens and the earth with truth; exalted is He above what they associate with Him﴾.

Know that when He, exalted is He, had made clear earlier that knowing the Truth for its own sake, which is what is meant by His saying ﴿that there is no god but I, so fear Me﴾, and knowing the good for the sake of acting upon it, which is what is meant by His saying ﴿so fear Me﴾, are the spirit of spirits, the rising point of felicities, and the source of goods and honours, He followed this with mention of the proofs of the existence of the Creator, the God, exalted is He, and of the perfection of His power and wisdom.

Know that we have explained that the proofs of divine matters (al-Ilahiyyat) are either by way of contingency (al-imkan) in essences or in attributes, or by way of origination (al-huduth) in essences or in attributes, or by way of the combination of contingency and origination in essences or attributes. These are six methods. The method mentioned in the revealed Books of God, exalted is He, is the argument from the origination of attributes and the changes of states. This method occurs in two ways:

The first: that one argues from what is more evident to what is more evident, ascending gradually to what is less evident. This is the method mentioned at the beginning of Surat al-Baqarah, for He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Worship your Lord, who created you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 21], so He made the change in the states of each person's own self a proof of his need for the Creator. Then He mentioned, after this, the argument from the states of the fathers and mothers, and to this refers His saying: ﴿and those before you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 21]. Then He mentioned, after this, the argument from the states of the earth, which is His saying: ﴿who made the earth a bed for you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 22], because the earth is nearer to us than the heaven. Then He mentioned at the fourth rank His saying: ﴿and the heaven as a canopy﴾ [al-Baqarah: 22]. Then He mentioned at the fifth rank the states that arise from the combination of the heaven with the earth, so He said: ﴿and sent down water from the heaven, and brought forth thereby fruits as a provision for you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 22].

The second of the Qur'anic proofs: that God, exalted is He, argues from the most noble to the most noble, descending to the lower and the lowest. This method is the one mentioned in this Surah, because He, exalted is He, began in arguing for the existence of the Chooser God by mentioning the lofty celestial bodies. Then He doubled (thanna) by mentioning the argument from the states of man, then tripled (thallatha) by mentioning the argument from the states of animals, then quadrupled (rabba'a) by mentioning the argument from the states of plants, then quintupled (khammasa) by mentioning the argument from the states of the four elements. This ordering is most excellent.

Once you have understood this introduction, we say:

The first type of the proofs mentioned for the existence of the Wise God is the argument from the states of the heavens and the earth. So He said: ﴿He created the heavens and the earth with truth; exalted is He above what they associate with Him﴾. We have already mentioned, in the commentary on His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Praise be to God, who created the heavens and the earth﴾ [al-An'am: 1], that the word khalq (creation) indicates the need for the Wise Creator in many respects, and there is no harm in repeating those respects here. We say: khalq is an expression for determining something by a specific measure, and this meaning is found in the heavens in several respects:

The first: every finite body is finite, and the body of the heaven is finite. Whatever is finite in size and extent, its being specifically in that determined quantity rather than more or less is a permissible matter, and whatever is permissible needs a determiner and a specifier, and whatever is in need of another is originated.

The second: the eternal motion is impossible, because motion requires being preceded by something else, and eternity negates this. So combining motion and eternity is impossible.

Once this is established, we say: either it is said that the bodies and masses were non-existent in eternity and then came into being, or it is said that although they existed in eternity, they were at rest and then moved. On both assumptions, their motion has a beginning, so the occurrence of motion at that starting point rather than before or after it is a creation and a determination, and therefore it requires a determiner, a creator and a specifier for it.

The third: the body of the sphere is composed of parts, some of which are situated in the depth of the mass of the sphere and some on its surface. What is situated in the depth could be conceived to be situated on the surface, and vice versa. Once this is established, the specification of each part to its determined place is a permissible matter, and so it requires a specifier and a determiner. The remaining respects are mentioned at the beginning of Surat al-An'am.

Know that when He, glorified is He, argued by creation and determination for the origination of the heavens and the earth, He said after it: ﴿exalted is He above what they associate with Him﴾. The meaning is that those who hold the heavens and the earth to be eternal are, as it were, attributing a partner to God in being eternal and everlasting, so He declared Himself exempt from that and made clear that none is eternal except Him. With this clarification it becomes evident that the purpose sought from His saying ﴿glorified is He, exalted is He above what they associate with Him﴾ at the beginning of the Surah is different from the purpose sought from mentioning this expression here. For the aim there is to refute the view of those who say that the idols intercede for the disbelievers to avert punishment from them, whereas the aim here is to refute the view of those who say: the bodies are eternal, and the heavens and the earth are everlasting. So God, glorified is He, declared Himself exempt from having anyone share with Him in eternity and pre-eternity. And God knows best.

The commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 16, verse 4:

Allah's words: ﴿He created man from a drop of fluid, and behold, he is an open adversary.﴾

Know that, after the spheres and the stars, the most noble of bodies is the human being. When Allah, exalted is He, cited the proof of the existence of the Wise God from the bodies of the spheres, He followed it with mention of the proof of this matter from the human being.

Know that the human being is composed of a body and a soul (nafs). Allah's words ﴿He created man from a drop of fluid﴾ point to the proof from his body for the existence of the Wise Creator, and His words ﴿and behold, he is an open adversary﴾ point to the proof from the states of his soul for the existence of the Wise Creator.

[p. 179]

As for the first method, its exposition is that we say: there is no doubt that the sperm-drop (nutfah) is a body whose parts are similar according to sense and observation. However, some physicians say that it is in reality composed of parts that differ, because it is only generated from the residue of the fourth digestion (al-hadm al-rabi'). Food undergoes a first digestion in the stomach, a second in the liver, and a third in the veins, and when it reaches the essential substances of the organs, a fourth digestion occurs. At this stage, some parts of the nourishment have reached the bone, and an effect of the bony nature has appeared in it. The same is said of the flesh, the sinews, the veins and other tissues. Then, when heat takes over the body at the arousal of desire, a melting occurs from among all the organs, and that is the sperm-drop. On this assumption, the sperm-drop is a body whose parts and natures differ.

Having understood this, we say: the sperm-drop in itself is either a body whose parts are similar in nature and quiddity, or a body whose parts differ. If the truth is the first, then it is not possible that what brings about the generation of the body from it is the nature present in the substance of the sperm-drop and the blood of menstruation. For nature acts essentially and by necessity, not by deliberate planning and choice. When a natural force acts upon a matter whose parts are similar, its action must be the sphere (al-kurah, the spherical shape). On this principle the philosophers relied in their statement that the simple bodies must have their natural shapes as spheres. Therefore, if what brings about the generation of the animal from the sperm-drop were nature, its shape would have to be a sphere. Since the matter is not so, we know that what brings about the coming-into-being of animal bodies is not nature, but a choosing agent, who creates by wisdom, planning and choice.

As for the second division, which is that the sperm-drop is a body composed of parts differing in nature and quiddity: we say, on the assumption that the matter is so, it must be that the generation of the body from it occurs by the planning of a choosing, wise agent. Its explanation is in several aspects:

The first aspect: the sperm-drop is a moisture that changes quickly. When it is so, the parts present in it do not preserve their position and arrangement. The part which is the matter of the brain may come to be located below, and the part which is the matter of the heart may come to be located above. When this is so, the organs of the animal could not be in this specific order as a constant or even a predominant matter. Since this is the case, we know that the coming-into-being of these organs in this specific order is only by the planning of the choosing, wise agent.

The second aspect: the sperm-drop, on the assumption that it is a body composed of parts differing in natures, must have its analysis of composition end in parts each of which is in itself a simple body. When this is so, if its manager were a natural force, each one of those simple parts would have to have the sphere as its shape, and so the animal would be in the shape of spheres joined one to another. Since the matter is not so, we know that the manager of animal bodies is not the natures, nor the influences of the stars and spheres, because those influences are similar. We therefore know that the manager of animal bodies is a choosing, wise agent, and this is what was sought. This is the proof from animal bodies for the existence of the choosing God. It is the meaning of His, glorified and exalted is He, words ﴿He created man from a drop of fluid﴾.

As for the proof for the existence of the choosing, wise Creator from the states of the human soul, it is the meaning of His words ﴿and behold, he is an open adversary﴾. Concerning it there are issues:

The first issue: explaining the manner and exposition of the proof. The human souls at the beginning of the natural disposition (fitrah) are less in understanding, intelligence and perceptiveness than the souls of the other animals. Do you not see that the chick, as soon as it emerges from the eggshell, distinguishes between the enemy and the friend, so it flees from the cat and seeks refuge with the mother, and it distinguishes between the food that suits it and the food that does not suit it? As for the human infant, when it is separated from the mother's womb, it does not at all distinguish between enemy and friend, nor between harmful and beneficial. It is therefore evident that the human being at the beginning of his coming-into-being is in a worse condition and less perceptive than the other animals. Then, after he grows up, his intellect becomes strong, his understanding increases, and he becomes capable of measuring the heavens and the earth, of knowing the essence and attributes of Allah, and of knowing the kinds of created things, spiritual and corporeal, celestial and elemental. He becomes capable of raising strong doubts concerning the religion of Allah, exalted is He, and of fierce disputes concerning every question. Thus, the transition of the human soul from that extreme dullness to this extreme shrewdness must necessarily be by the planning of a choosing, wise God, who transports the spirits from their deficiency to their perfections, and from their ignorance to their knowledge, according to wisdom and choice. This is what is meant by His, glorified and exalted is He, words ﴿He created man from a drop of fluid, and behold, he is an open adversary﴾.

Once you have understood this subtle point, you can be alerted to many aspects.

The second issue: He, exalted is He, creates man from the sperm-drop only through many changes mentioned in the Noble Qur'an, among them His, exalted is He, words: ﴿And We created man from an extract of clay. Then We placed him as a sperm-drop in a secure place.﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 12–13]. However, He, exalted is He, abridged here because that detailed account is mentioned in other verses. His words ﴿and behold, he is an open adversary﴾ contain two investigations:

The first investigation: al-Wahidi said: khasim means mukhasim (one who disputes). The lexicographers said: khasimuka is the one who disputes with you. The form fa'il in the sense of mufa'il is well known, as in nasib in the sense of munasib, 'ashir in the sense of mu'ashir, and akil and sharib. It is also permissible that khasim be an agent noun from khasama, yakhsimu, in the sense of ikhtasama (to dispute). From this is the recitation of Hamzah (one of the seven canonical readers): ﴿taʾkhudhuhum wa hum yakhsimun﴾ [Ya Sin: 49] (a recitation variant reading the verb as yakhsimun).

The second investigation: His words ﴿and behold, he is an open adversary﴾ have two possible meanings:

One of them: then, behold, he is one who argues, disputing on behalf of himself, contending with the adversaries, after having been a filthy sperm-drop and an inanimate matter with neither sensation nor motion. The purpose of this is that the transition from that base state to this lofty, noble state does not occur except by the planning of a wise, all-knowing manager.

The second: then, behold, he is an adversary against his Lord, denying his Creator, saying: ﴿Who will give life to bones when they are decayed?﴾ [Ya Sin: 78]. The purpose of this is to describe man with extreme impudence and ignorance, and persistence in ingratitude for the blessing. The first meaning is more fitting, because these verses are mentioned to establish the manner of the proof for the existence of the Wise Creator, not to establish the impudence of people and their persistence in disbelief and ingratitude.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 16, verses 5–7:

Allah the Exalted says: "And the cattle—He created them for you; in them is warmth and benefits, and from them you eat. And for you in them is beauty when you bring them home at evening and when you send them out to pasture. And they carry your loads to a land you could not reach except with great hardship to yourselves. Indeed, your Lord is Kind and Merciful."

There are several issues here.

**Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 16, verse 8:**

God, exalted is He, says: ﴿And horses, mules and donkeys, for you to ride and as adornment.﴾ On this verse there are several issues.

**First issue:** His saying ﴿and horses, mules and donkeys﴾ is coordinated with (*'ataf*) the cattle (*al-an'am*). That is, He created the cattle for such-and-such purposes, and He created these things for riding. His saying ﴿and as adornment﴾ means: and He created them as adornment. A parallel to this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We adorned the lowest heaven with lamps and as a protection﴾ [Fussilat: 12], meaning: and We protected it with protection. Al-Zajjaj said: ﴿and as adornment﴾ is in the accusative because it is an object of purpose (*maf'ul lahu*). The meaning is: and He created them for adornment.

**Second issue:** Those who hold that eating horse meat is forbidden have argued from this verse. They said: the benefit of eating is greater than the benefit of riding. So if eating horse meat were permissible, this benefit would have been more appropriate to mention. Since God, exalted is He, did not mention it, we know that eating it is forbidden. This argument can also be strengthened from another angle: God, exalted is He, said concerning the cattle: ﴿and from them you eat﴾, and this expression (*kalimah*) conveys restriction (*hasr*). It therefore requires that eating from anything other than the cattle is not permissible. So the eating of horse meat must be forbidden by the implication of this restriction. Furthermore, after this statement, God, exalted is He, mentioned the horses, mules and donkeys and stated that they were created for riding. This requires that the benefit of eating is restricted to the cattle and is not present in these things. The verse can be used as an argument from a third angle, namely that His saying ﴿for you to ride them﴾ requires that the complete purpose of creating these three things is riding and adornment. Had eating them been permissible, the complete purpose of creating them would not be riding; rather, the permissibility of eating them would also be a purpose. In that case, the permissibility of riding them would no longer be the complete purpose but only part of it.

Al-Wahidi answered with a response of great excellence. He said: If this verse indicated the prohibition of eating these animals, the prohibition of eating them would have been known in Mecca, because this surah is Meccan. And if this were the case, then the view of the majority of the exegetes and the scholars of hadith that the flesh of domestic donkeys was prohibited on the day of Khaybar would be invalid. This is because, since the prohibition already existed before that day, singling out that prohibition with this doubt would serve no purpose. This is a sound and firm answer.

**Third issue:** Those who hold that the acts of God, exalted is He, are caused by interests and wisdoms (*al-qa'ilun bi-ta'lil af'al Allah bi-l-masalih wa-l-hikam*) argued from the apparent meaning of this verse, for it requires that these animals were created for the sake of such-and-such benefit. A parallel to this is His saying: ﴿A Book We have sent down to you that you may bring mankind out of darkness into light﴾ [Ibrahim: 1], and His saying: ﴿And I did not create jinn and humankind except that they worship Me﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 56]. The discussion of this is well known.

**Fourth issue:** Someone may say: since the meaning of the verse is that God, exalted is He, created the horses, mules and donkeys for you to ride them, and so that they would be an adornment for you, why did He leave out this expression?

Its answer is that if God, exalted is He, had mentioned this matter in this form, the meaning would be that adornment by them is one of the considered purposes. That is impermissible, because adornment with a thing produces self-admiration, arrogance and pride, and these are blameworthy traits which God, exalted is He, has forbidden and warned against. How, then, could He say: "I created these animals to achieve these meanings"? Rather, He said: He created them for you to ride, so that through them you may ward off from yourselves the harm of exhaustion and hardship. As for adornment by them, it is present in reality, but it is not an intended purpose in itself. This is the benefit of choosing this expression.

Alternatively: know that when God, exalted is He, first mentioned the conditions of the animals from which humans benefit in an essential way, and second the conditions of the animals from which humans benefit in a non-essential way, a third category of animals remained, namely those from which humans generally do not benefit. So He mentioned them in summary, saying: ﴿and He creates what you do not know﴾. This is because their kinds, types and categories are numerous and beyond limit and enumeration. If a person were to delve into explaining the wonders of their conditions, what was mentioned would, after writing many volumes, be like a drop in the sea. So the best way to mention them is in summary, as God, exalted is He, did in this verse.

Ata, Muqatil and al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: On the right side of the Throne is a river of light, equal to the seven heavens, the seven earths and the seven seas. Jibril (peace be upon him) enters it every dawn and bathes, and he increases in light upon his light and in beauty upon his beauty. Then he shakes himself, and from every drop that falls from his feathers God creates so-and-so thousands of angels. Of them, seventy thousand enter the Bayt al-Ma'mur (the Frequented House, in the heavens) each day, and seventy thousand enter the Ka'bah as well. Then they do not return to it until the Hour is established.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 16, verses 9–10:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And upon Allah is the direction of the way, and among the ways is that which deviates. And if He willed, He would have guided you all.﴾

Know that when He, exalted is He, had explained the proofs of tawhid, He said: ﴿And upon Allah is the direction of the way﴾, meaning: I only mentioned these proofs and explained them to remove the excuse and eliminate the pretext, so that whoever perishes perishes by clear evidence, and whoever lives lives by clear evidence. There are several issues concerning the verse:

The first issue: al-Wahidi said: al-qasd (direction) is the straightness of the path. It is said: "a qasd path" (ṭarīq qaṣd) and "qāṣid" when it leads you to your goal. Knowing this, there is an ellipsis in the verse, and the sense is: "And upon Allah is the explanation of the direction of the way." Then He said: ﴿and among the ways is that which deviates﴾, meaning: jā'ir, that which inclines away (ʿādil māʾil). The meaning of jawr (deviation) in the language is inclining away from the truth. The pronoun in His saying ﴿and among them is jā'ir﴾ refers to the way (al-sabīl), and it is feminine in the dialect of the Ḥijāz. That is, among the ways is that which is deviant, not directed toward the truth, and this is the various kinds of disbelief and misguidance. And Allah knows best.

The second issue: The Muʿtazilah said: the verse indicates that it is obligatory upon Allah, exalted is He, to give guidance and direction to the religion, and to remove pretexts and excuses, because He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And upon Allah is the direction of the way﴾, and the word ʿalā (upon) denotes obligation, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And for Allah, upon the people, is the pilgrimage to the House﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 97]. The verse also indicates that He, exalted is He, does not lead anyone astray, nor misguide him, nor turn him away from it, because if He were the doer of misguidance, He would have said: ﴿And upon Allah is the direction of the way﴾ and "upon Him is its deviating," or He would have said: "upon Him is the deviant." Since He did not say that, but said regarding the direction of the way that it is upon Him, and did not say regarding the deviation of the way that it is upon Him, but said: ﴿and among them is jā'ir﴾, this indicates that He, exalted is He, does not lead anyone astray from the religion.

Our companions answered that the intended meaning is that it is upon Allah, according to His bounty and generosity, to make clear the true religion and the correct creed. As for making clear the manner of misguidance and leading astray, that is not obligatory. This is what is meant, and Allah knows best.

The third issue: His saying: ﴿And if He willed, He would have guided you all﴾ indicates that He, exalted is He, did not will the guidance of the disbelievers, and did not intend faith from them, because the word (law, "if") indicates the absence of one thing due to the absence of another. His saying ﴿And if He willed to guide you﴾ means: if He had willed your guidance, He would have guided you. This indicates that He, exalted is He, did not will their guidance, so they were not guided. This indicates the intended point.

al-Aṣamm answered regarding it that the meaning is: if He had willed to compel you to faith, He would have guided you. This indicates that the will of compulsion did not occur.

al-Jubbaʾi answered that the meaning is: and if He had willed, He would have guided you to Paradise and to attaining reward; but He does not do that except for one who deserves it, and He did not intend by it guidance to faith, because that is within the capacity of all the accountable.

Some answered, saying the intended meaning is: and if He had willed, He would have guided you to Paradise from the outset, by way of grace; but He, exalted is He, made you aware of the great rank through the proofs He established and made clear. Whoever holds fast to them attains those ranks, and whoever turns away from them misses them and goes to punishment. And Allah knows best.

Know that these statements have been mentioned by us several times and in various forms along with the answers, so there is no benefit in repeating them.

[Page 186]

The statement of the Exalted: ﴿He it is who sent down water from the sky; from it is drink, and from it are trees in which you pasture [your livestock].﴾ ﴿He causes to grow for you thereby crops, olives, date palms, and grapes, and of all the fruits. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who reflect.﴾

Know that after animals, the noblest of the bodies of the lower world is plant life. When God, exalted is He, established the argument (istidlal, inference from evidence) for the existence of the Wise Creator through the wondrous states of animals, He followed it in this verse with mention of the argument for the existence of the Wise Creator through the wondrous states of plants.

Know that the water sent down from the sky is rain. As for whether rain descends from the clouds or from the sky, we have mentioned this in this book many times. The summary is that rainwater is of two kinds:

The first is that which God, exalted is He, made a drink for us and for every living creature. This is what is meant by His words: ﴿from it is drink﴾. God, exalted is He, has made clear in another verse that this blessing is great, saying: ﴿And We made from water every living thing﴾ [al-Anbiya': 30].

If it is said: Do you claim that the drinking of creatures is only from rain, or do you say that it may be from rain and may be from something else, namely the water present in the depths of the earth?

The Qadi (the judge) answered: God, exalted is He, has made clear that rain is our drink, and He did not deny that we may drink from something else.

One may say: The apparent sense of the verse indicates restriction (hasr, exclusivity), because His words ﴿from it is drink﴾ convey restriction, since their meaning is: from it, not from anything else.

Given this, we say: It is not impossible that sweet water beneath the earth is part of the rainwater that settles there. The evidence for this is His words, exalted is He, in Surat al-Mu'minun: ﴿And We sent down from the sky water in measure, then We made it dwell in the earth﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 18]. Nor is it impossible that salt water, which is the sea, is also part of the rainwater.

The second kind of water descending from the sky is that which God makes a means for the growth of plants. To this refers His words: ﴿and from it are trees in which you pasture [your livestock]﴾ to the end of the verse. There are issues to discuss in this.

First issue: The apparent sense of this verse requires that grazing of trees (isamah, letting livestock graze freely) be possible. This is valid only if by "trees" (shajar) is meant pasture and herbage. There are two opinions:

The first opinion: al-Zajjaj said: Everything that is firmly rooted in the earth is a shajar (tree). He recited:

"He feeds them meat when shajar (pasture) is scarce."

He means: they give the horses milk when the land is barren. Ibn Qutaybah said concerning this verse: The intended meaning of shajar is pasture. In the hadith of Ikrimah: "Do not eat the price of shajar, for it is unlawful (suht)," he means: pasture.

One may say: He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And the star and the tree prostrate﴾ [al-Rahman: 6], and the intended meaning of "star" is what grows from the earth without a stalk, while the intended meaning of "tree" is what has a stalk. Thus said the exegetes. In sum, since He joined the tree to the star by conjunction, this indicates that the two are distinct. This may be answered by saying that conjoining a genus with a species, and the reverse, is well known. Also, the word shajar implies mixing (ikhtilat), as one says: "tasha-jara al-qawm" when the voices of some of them mix with others, and "tasha-jarat al-rimah" when the spears become intermixed. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿until they make you judge in what is disputed (shajara) between them﴾ [al-Nisa': 65]. The sense of mixing is present in herbage and pasture, so it is necessary that the word shajar be permissible to apply to it.

The second opinion: Camels are able to graze on the leaves of large trees. On this reading, there is no need for what we mentioned in the first opinion.

Second issue: His words ﴿in which you pasture﴾ mean: in the trees you pasture your livestock. One says: "asamtu al-mashiyah" when I let the livestock graze freely, and the livestock themselves "sama" (roam and graze) when they graze wherever they wish; they are then sawam and sa'imah. Al-Zajjaj said: It is taken from al-sawmah, which is a mark, and its interpretation is that by grazing they leave marks on the earth. Others said: Because they are set loose for pasturing. The full discussion of this term we have mentioned in Surat Al 'Imran, in His words: ﴿and the marked horses﴾ [Al 'Imran: 14].

As for His words, exalted is He: ﴿He causes to grow for you thereby crops, olives, date palms, and grapes﴾, there are issues here:

First issue: The plants that God causes to grow from the water of the sky are of two kinds:

One kind is prepared for the pasturing of cattle and the grazing of animals, and this is what is meant by His words: ﴿in which you pasture﴾.

The second kind is that which was created for human food, and this is what is meant by His words: ﴿He causes to grow for you thereby crops, olives﴾.

If it is said: In this verse God began with mention of what is pasture for animals and followed it with mention of what is food for humans, whereas in another verse He reversed this order, beginning with mention of human food and then what the rest of the animals graze, saying: ﴿Eat and pasture your livestock﴾ [Ta-Ha: 54]. What is the benefit in this?

We say: As for the order mentioned in this verse, it alerts to noble character, namely that a person's concern for those under his hand should be more complete than his concern for his own state. As for the order mentioned in the other verse, the purpose of it is what is mentioned in his (ﷺ) saying: "Begin with yourself, then with those you support."

Second issue: 'Asim, in the transmission of Abu Bakr, read (nunbitu) with the nun, for emphasis (tafkhim), while the rest read it with the ya'. al-Wahidi said: The ya' is more consistent with what precedes.

Third issue: Know that man was created needing food, and food is either from animals or from plants. Animal food is more noble than plant food, because the formation of human body parts from eating animal parts is easier than their formation from eating plants, since the resemblance there is more complete and perfect. Animal food is obtained only through the grazing of animals and the effort to multiply them by means of pasturing, and this is what God mentioned in the grazing. As for plant food, it is of two kinds: grains and fruits. Grains are indicated by the word "crops" (zar'), and fruits are the noblest of which are olives, date palms, and grapes. As for the olive, it is a fruit in one respect and a condiment in another, because of the abundance of oil in it, and the benefits of oils are many in eating, in anointing, and in lighting lamps. As for the distinction of date palms and grapes from all other fruits, it is clear and well known.

Just as God, exalted is He, when He mentioned the animals from which people benefit in detail, then said in describing the rest: ﴿And He creates what you do not know﴾, so too here, when He mentioned the kinds of plants from which benefit is derived, He said in describing the rest: ﴿and of all the fruits﴾, to alert that detailing their kinds, species, attributes, and benefits cannot be mentioned in volumes; so it is better to limit oneself here to a summary statement.

Then He said: ﴿Indeed in that is a sign for a people who reflect.﴾ Here there are two discussions:

First discussion: Explaining how these things are signs indicating the existence of God, exalted is He. We say: A single seed falls into the mud, and when it remains in this state for determined periods of time, parts of the earth's moisture and dampness penetrate inside that seed, so the seed swells and both its top and bottom split. From the top of the seed emerges a tree rising from inside the earth into the air, and from its bottom emerges another tree plunging into the depths of the earth, and this plunging one is what is called the roots of the tree. Then that tree continues to increase, grow, and strengthen, and from it emerge leaves, blossoms, sheaths, and fruits. Then that fruit contains bodies of differing natures, such as the grape: its skin and its seeds are cold, dry, and dense, while its flesh and its water are hot, moist, and subtle.

Once you know this, we say: The relation of the lower natures to this body is similar, and the relation of celestial influences and stellar motions to the whole is similar. Despite the similarity of the relations of these things, you see these bodies differing in nature, taste, color, scent, and quality. Clear reason therefore indicates that this is only for the sake of an agent who is powerful, wise, and merciful. This is the framing of this proof.

Second discussion: God, exalted is He, concluded this verse with His words: ﴿for a people who reflect﴾. The reason for this is that He mentioned that He ﴿sent down water from the sky, and thereby caused to grow crops, olives, date palms, and grapes﴾.

One may say: We do not grant that it is He, exalted is He, who caused them to grow. Why could it not be said that these things came into being and were generated by the succession of the four seasons and the influences of the sun, the moon, and the stars? Once you have understood this objection, then as long as no proof has been established for the invalidity of this possibility, this proof is not complete and sufficient to establish this claim, and the place of thought and contemplation remains open. For this reason He concluded this verse with His words: ﴿for a people who reflect﴾.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 16, verses 12–13:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And He has subjected to you the night and the day, and the sun and the moon; and the stars are subjected by His command. Indeed in that are signs for a people who use reason.﴾ ﴿And what He has created for you on the earth of various colours. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who take heed.﴾

On the verse there are several issues:

The first issue: Know that when Allah, exalted is He, in this verse answered the question we mentioned, He did so in two ways:

The first: We say that the occurrence of events in this lower world is ascribed to the celestial connections and the stellar configurations. However, their movements and connections must have causes, and the causes of those movements are either their own essences or matters other than them. The first is invalid, for two reasons:

The first: Bodies are alike. So if one body were the cause of a attribute, every body would necessarily have that attribute, and this is impossible.

The second: If the essence of a body were the cause of the occurrence of this portion of motion, then this portion of motion would have to persist as long as that essence persists. If that were so, the body would have to remain in one state without any change at all, and this entails that it is at rest and prevents it from being in motion. So it is established that the claim that a body is moving by its essence entails that it is at rest by its essence, and whatever leads its affirmation to its negation is invalid. Thus it is established that a body cannot be moving by virtue of being a body, so it remains that it is moving by something other than itself. That other either inheres in it or is separate from it. The first is invalid, because the same discussion recurs: that this very body was specifically singled out with this very power, rather than the rest of bodies. Thus it is established that the movers of the bodies of the spheres and the stars are matters separate from them. And that separate thing, if it is a body or corporeal, the first division recurs regarding it; and if it is neither a body nor corporeal, then it is either an essentially causative agent or a free, choosing agent. The first is invalid, because the relation of that essentially causative agent to all bodies is equal, so no body is more fitted than another to receive some specific effects. Since this has been shown invalid, it is established that the mover of the spheres and stars is the free, powerful agent, transcendent above being a body or corporeal, and that is Allah, exalted is He. The summary is: even if we judge that the events of the lower world are ascribed to the celestial and stellar motions, these celestial and stellar motions cannot be ascribed to other spheres, for otherwise an infinite regress would follow, which is impossible. So the creator and governor of these motions must be Allah, exalted is He. And since the lower events are ascribed to the celestial motions, and it is established that the celestial motions are originated by the creation, decree and origination of Allah, exalted is He, this is an acknowledgment that everything is from Allah, exalted is He, and by His origination and creation. This is what is meant by His saying: ﴿And He has subjected to you the night and the day, and the sun and the moon﴾, meaning: if those lower events are on account of the alternation of night and day and the motions of the sun and moon, then these things must certainly have their occurrence by the creation and subjection of Allah, exalted is He, to avoid an infinite regress. And since this argument is complete in this context, He therefore concluded this verse with His saying: ﴿Indeed in that are signs for a people who use reason﴾, meaning: every one who is rational knows that the claim of an infinite regress is invalid, and in the end one must arrive at the free, powerful agent. This is the statement of one of the two answers.

The second answer to that question: We say: We establish the proof that the occurrence of plants and animals cannot be due to the influence of natures, spheres and stars. This is because the influence of natures, spheres, stars, the sun and the moon is one and the same with respect to all things. Then we see that when a grape is produced, its skin has one nature, its seed another nature, its flesh a third nature, and its water a fourth nature. Indeed, we see in the rose that one face of a single leaf is in extreme yellowness, while the other face of that same leaf is in extreme redness, and that leaf is in extreme thinness and delicacy. We know by necessity that the relation of the stars and spheres to the two faces of that thin leaf is one and the same relation. And one nature in one matter produces only one effect. Do you not see that they said: the shape of the simple body is the sphere, because the influence of one nature on one matter must be uniform, and the shape whose all sides are alike is the sphere. Also, if we place wax, and five cubits of that wax are lit on one side, then a similar effect must occur on all sides, because the influencing nature must have a uniform relation to all sides.

Given this, we say: it is clear that the relation of the sun, moon, stars, spheres and natures to the two faces of that fine, thin leaf is one and the same relation. And it is established that when the influencing nature has one relation, the effect is uniform. And it is established that the effect is not uniform, because one face of that leaf is in extreme yellowness while the other face is in extreme redness. This indicates with certainty that the influencer in producing these attributes, colours and states is not nature, but the free, wise agent, who is Allah, glorified and exalted is He. This is what is meant by His saying: ﴿And what He has created for you on the earth of various colours﴾.

Know that since the basis of this argument is that an influencer that is essentially and naturally causative must have one and the same relation to all things, then when the senses show in these plant bodies the difference of their attributes and the variance of their states, it becomes clear that the influencer in them is not essentially necessary but a free agent. This is the complete statement of these proofs. It is established that the concluding of the first verse with His saying: ﴿for a people who reflect﴾, the second verse with His saying: ﴿for a people who use reason﴾, and the third verse with His saying: ﴿for a people who take heed﴾, is what draws attention to these precious benefits and clear proofs. Praise be to Allah for His kindnesses in religion and in this world.

The second issue: Ibn ʿAmir recited (wal-shamsu wal-qamaru wal-nujumu), all of them in the nominative case, as inceptive (mubtada'), with the predicate being His saying (musakhkharatun). Hafs from ʿAsim recited ﴿wal-nujumu﴾ in the nominative, so that His saying ﴿wal-nujumu﴾ is an inceptive. He was led to this only so that the word for subjection would not be repeated, since the Arabs do not say "I subjected this thing, subjected." Its answer is that the meaning is that He, exalted is He, subjected these things for us while they are subjected under His power and will. This is the sound statement, and the sense: He, exalted is He, subjected these things for mankind and made them suited to their interests while they are subjected under the power, command and permission of Allah, exalted is He. On this interpretation, the repetition devoid of benefit is not necessary. And Allah knows best.

Questions remain concerning the verse:

The first question: Taskhir (subjection) is an expression for compulsion and forcing, and this is fitting only for one who is capable and can compel. How then is this valid regarding night and day, and regarding inanimate things, the sun and the moon?

The answer is in two ways:

The first: When He arranged these things in one manner conforming to the interests of the servants, they became like an obedient, submissive servant. For this reason, this kind of arrangement was termed subjection.

As for the second answer: it holds only according to the doctrine of the astronomers. They say: the natural motion of the sun and the moon is the motion from west to east, and Allah moves these stars by means of the motion of the greatest sphere from east to west. So this motion is forced, and for this reason the word "taskhir" was used regarding it.

The second question: If the occurrence of night and day comes about only through the motions of the sun, then mentioning night and day would suffice without mentioning the sun.

The answer: the occurrence of day and night is not due to the motion of the sun; rather, their occurrence is due to the motion of the greatest sphere, whose motion we have shown is nothing but by the motion of Allah, glorified is He. As for the motion of the sun, it is the cause of the occurrence of the year, not of the day.

The third question: What is the meaning of His saying ﴿subjected by His command﴾, when the one who effects subjection is power, not command?

The answer: this verse is based on whether the spheres and stars are inanimate or not. Most Muslims hold that they are inanimate, and therefore they interpreted the command in this verse as creation and decree. The word "amr" with the meaning of affair and act occurs frequently; He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Our word to a thing, when We intend it, is only that We say to it "Be," and it is﴾ [al-Nahl: 40]. Some people say that they are not inanimate, and in that case the command is interpreted as permission and obligation. And Allah knows best.
