The first: He said, ﴿if Allah were to take mankind to task for their wrongdoing﴾, attributing wrongdoing to all of mankind. Without doubt, wrongdoing is among the sins, so this requires that every human being commits sin and disobedience. The second: He, exalted is He, said: ﴿He would not leave upon its back a single creature﴾. This requires that everyone on the surface of the earth is committing wrongdoing and sin, so that the destruction of every wrongdoer would entail the destruction of all mankind.

But if we say that the prophets, peace be upon them, did not commit wrongdoing, then they need not be destroyed, and so the destruction of all the wrongdoers would not entail the destruction of all mankind, nor would no creature remain on the surface of the earth. Since this entailment is invalid, we know that all human beings are wrongdoers, whether they are prophets or not.

The answer: It has been established by evidence that not all people are wrongdoers, since He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Then We caused the Book to be inherited by those whom We chose from among Our servants; and among them is one who wrongs himself, and among them is one who is moderate, and among them is one who is foremost in good deeds﴾ [Fatir: 32]. If the moderate and the foremost were wrongdoers, that division would collapse. So we know that the moderate and the foremost are not wrongdoers. Thus it is established by this evidence that it is not permissible to say that all creation are wrongdoers.

Given this, we say: the people mentioned in His saying ﴿if Allah were to take mankind to task﴾ are either all the sinners deserving punishment, or those previously mentioned, namely the polytheists and those who attributed daughters to Allah. On this interpretation the argument falls. And Allah knows best.

Know that the discussion of these issues has been mentioned by us repeatedly, so we will not repeat it. And Allah knows best.

**The fourth issue:** The apparent meaning of the verse indicates that people's engaging in wrongdoing necessitates the destruction of all living creatures, and that is not permissible, because the creature has committed no sin. How then is it permissible to destroy it because of the wrongdoing of people?

The answer to this is in two ways:

The first way: We do not concede that His saying, ﴿He would not leave upon its back a single creature﴾, encompasses all living creatures. Abu ʿAli al-Jubbaʾi answered this: The meaning is that if Allah took them to task for what they earned of disbelief and disobedience, He would hasten their destruction, and then they would have no offspring. Then it is known that there is no one except that among his forefathers there is someone who deserves punishment. And if they perished, their progeny would be extinguished, so it would follow that no human being would remain in the world. And if they were extinguished, it would necessarily follow that no living creature would remain either, since living creatures were created for the benefit and welfare of the servants. This is a subtle and good answer.

The second way: If the calamity befalls the wrongdoers, it also befalls the rest of mankind and the animals. For the wrongdoers that calamity is a punishment, and for others it is a trial. This event occurred in the time of Noah, peace be upon him.

The third way: If He were to seize them, rain would cease, and with its cessation vegetation would cease, so no creature would remain upon its back. It is reported from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that he heard a man say: "The wrongdoer harms only himself." He said: "No, by Allah! Rather, the bustard (*ḥubārā*) in its nest dies because of the wrongdoing of the wrongdoer." And it is reported from Ibn Masʿud, may Allah be pleased with him: "The dung beetle nearly perished in its burrow because of the sin of the son of Adam." These three answers are based on the assumption that the word *dābbah* (creature) encompasses all living creatures.

The second answer: The meaning of His saying, ﴿He would not leave upon its back a single creature﴾, is: He would not leave upon its back a single disbeliever. So the word *dābbah* refers to the disbeliever. The evidence for this is His saying: ﴿Those are like livestock; rather, they are further astray﴾ [al-Araf: 179]. And Allah knows best.

\* \* \*

**The fifth issue:** The pronoun in His saying, ﴿upon it [ʿalayhā]﴾ refers to the earth, although it has not been previously mentioned. However, the mention of the creature indicates the earth, since the creature moves only upon it. It is very common to refer to the earth by a pronoun even when it has not been previously mentioned, because they say: "There is no one like so-and-so upon it" and "There is no one more noble than so-and-so upon it," meaning: upon the earth.

\* \* \*

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿But He defers them to a specified term﴾, so that they may reproduce. Regarding the interpretation of this term there are two views:

The first view: This is the view of ʿAṭāʾ, from Ibn ʿAbbas, that it refers to the term of the Resurrection.

The second view: That it means the end of their lifespan.

The reasoning of the first view: most of the punishment reaches them on the Day of Resurrection.

The reasoning of the second view: The polytheists are taken to task with punishment when their lifespans end and they depart from the world.

The third category of the false statements which the disbelievers used to make, and which Allah, the Exalted, related about them, is His saying: ﴿And they attribute to Allah what they dislike﴾.

Know that the meaning of His saying ﴿And they attribute [wa-yajʿalūna]﴾ is: the daughters, which they dislike for themselves. And the meaning of His saying ﴿they attribute﴾ is that they describe Allah with this and judge it for Him, like the saying: "I appointed Zayd over the people," meaning: I ruled with this ruling. We have mentioned the meaning of *jaʿl* (appointing/making) at His saying: ﴿Allah did not institute any *baḥīrah* or *sāʾibah*﴾ [al-Maʾidah: 103].

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And their tongues describe the lie that for them is the best﴾. Al-Farraʾ and al-Zajjaj said: The position of *anna* (أنَّ, "that") is in the accusative, because His saying ﴿that for them is the best﴾ is in apposition to *al-kadhib* (the lie), and the sentence is: "And their tongues describe that for them is the best."

Regarding the interpretation of "the best" (*al-ḥusnā*) here there are two views:

The first: What is meant by it is sons, meaning: they said: "For Allah are the daughters, and for us are the sons."

The second: That along with their assertion that daughters belong to Allah, the Exalted, they describe themselves as having gained the pleasure of Allah, the Exalted, through this statement, and that they are upon the true religion and the good path.

The third: that they judged for themselves paradise and reward from Allah, the Exalted.

If it is said: How can they judge this, when they were deniers of the Resurrection?

We say: Not all of them were deniers of the Resurrection. It has been said that among the Arabs there was a group who affirmed resurrection and the Day of Judgment, and for this reason they used to tie a precious camel at the grave of a dead person and leave it until it died, saying: "Indeed, that dead person, if..."

[Page 50]

...ḥushira fa-innahu yuḥsharu ma'ahu markūbuhu (he is gathered, and his mount is gathered with him). Also, on the assumption that they denied the Resurrection, they may have said: "If Muhammad is truthful in his claim of resurrection and gathering, then we shall obtain Paradise and reward through this true religion that we follow." Some people said: "It is preferable to take *al-ḥusnā* (the best reward) in this sense, as evidence by His saying after it: ﴿Undoubtedly, theirs is the Fire﴾. He thus rejected their claim and affirmed the Fire for them, which indicates that they had judged Paradise for themselves."

Al-Zajjāj said: "*Lā* (no) is a rejection of their statement, meaning: the matter is not as they describe. *Jarama* means: their act, that is, the earning of that statement, has brought them the Fire. On this reading, *anna* (that) is in the accusative position, governed by the action of earning upon it." Qutrub said: "*Anna* is in the nominative position, and the meaning is: it has become necessary that theirs is the Fire." Whatever the i'rab (grammatical analysis), the meaning is that the Fire is rightfully theirs, necessary and established.

As for His saying ﴿and that they are *mufraṭūn*﴾: Nāfi' and Qutayba, on the authority of al-Kisā'ī, read *mufriṭūn* with a kasra on the rā', while the rest read *mufraṭūn* with a fatḥa on the rā'. Regarding Nāfi''s reading, al-Farrā' said: the meaning is that they were *mufriṭīn* ("excessive") against themselves in sins. It was also said: they went to excess in fabricating lies against God. Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī said: it seems to derive from *afraṭa*, meaning he became one having *faraṭ* (precedence), like *ajraba* meaning he became one having *jarab* (scabies). The meaning is that they are those who have precedence toward the Fire, as if they had sent someone to prepare places for them therein.

As for the reading *mufraṭūn* with a fatḥa on the rā', there are two opinions:

The first opinion: the meaning is that they are *mutrakūn* (left behind) in the Fire. Al-Kisā'ī said: it is said, "I did not leave (*afraṭtu*) any one of the people," meaning, I did not leave any behind. Al-Farrā' said: the Arabs say, "I left (*afraṭtu*) people among them," meaning I left them behind and they were forgotten.

The second opinion: *mufraṭūn* means *mu'ajjalūn* (those hastened forward). Al-Wāḥidī, may God have mercy on him, said: this is the preferred view, and its basis is what Abū Zayd and others said: "*faraṭa al-rajulu aṣḥābahu yafrusuhum faraṭan wa furūṭan*," when he went ahead of them to the water to prepare the buckets and ropes; and "*afraṭa al-qawmu al-fārita wa farraṭūhu*" when they sent him ahead. So the meaning of His saying ﴿*mufraṭūn*﴾ on this interpretation is that they have been sent ahead to the Fire, and so they are a *faraṭ* (forerunner) for those who will enter after them.

Then God, exalted is He, explained that this kind of conduct which proceeds from the idolaters of Quraysh has previously proceeded from all the earlier nations regarding the earlier prophets, peace be upon them. He said: ﴿By God, We certainly sent [messengers] to nations before you, but Satan made their deeds seem fair to them﴾. This serves as consolation to the Messenger ﷺ regarding the grief he suffered because of the ignorance of his people.

The Mu'tazilah said: this verse indicates the falsity of the view of the Mujbirah (determinists) in several respects.

First: if the creator of their actions is God, Most High, then there is no benefit in the "making fair."

Second: since that adornment is by the creation of God, Most High, it is not permissible to blame Satan for it.

Third: the adornment is what calls a person to the act, and if the occurrence of the act in him is by the creation of God, Most High, then it is necessary, and so the adornment would not be a calling.

Fourth: on their view, the Creator of that deed is more worthy to be their patron than the one who calls to it.

Fifth: He, Most High, attributed the adornment to Satan, and if the one adorning were God, Most High, then attributing it to Satan would be a lie.

The answer: if the one who beautifies the ugly things in the eyes of the disbelievers is Satan, then if the one who beautifies those whisperings in the eyes of Satan is another satan, an infinite regress (*tasalsul*) follows. And if it is God, Most High, then that is what is sought.

Then God, Most High, said: ﴿So he is their patron today﴾, and in this there are two possibilities:

The first: what is meant is the disbelievers of Mecca, and by His saying ﴿so he is their patron today﴾ is meant: Satan, who takes charge of misguiding them and turning them away from you, just as he did with the disbelievers of the nations before you. On this interpretation, He has turned from reports about the earlier nations to reports about the disbelievers of Mecca.

The second: by "today" He intended the Day of Resurrection. The meaning is: he is the patron of those who disbelieved, adorning their deeds for them on the Day of Resurrection. The name "the day" was applied to the Day of Resurrection because of the fame of that day.

[Page 51]

And what is intended by His saying ﴿so he is their patron today﴾ is that they will have no patron or helper on that day. That is because when they witness the punishment, and Satan too has been struck by it just as it has struck them, and they see that he has no way of escape from it just as they have none, they may be rebuked by being told, mockingly: "This is your patron today."

* * *

Then God, Most High, mentioned that alongside this severe threat, He established the proof and removed the excuse, saying: ﴿And We have not sent down to you the Book except that you may make clear to them that over which they differ, and as guidance and mercy﴾. In this there are several issues:

The first issue: the meaning is: We have not sent down the Qur'an to you except that you may, through the clarifications of this Qur'an, make clear to them the matters over which they differ. Those who differ are the people of the religions and the sects, and what they differ over is religion, such as monotheism and polytheism, determinism and free will, the affirmation and denial of the Return, and likewise rulings, such as their prohibiting things that are permitted, like the *baḥīrah* and the *sā'ibah* and others, and their permitting things that are forbidden, like carrion.

The second issue: the *lām* in His saying ﴿that you may make clear﴾ indicates that the acts of God, Most High, are caused by purposes. A similar verse is His saying: ﴿A Book which We have sent down to you that you may bring mankind out...﴾ [Ibrahim: 1], and His saying: ﴿I did not create the jinn and humankind except that they may worship Me﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 56].

The answer: since it has been established by reason that causation is impossible, it is necessary to turn it to interpretation (*ta'wīl*).

The third issue: the author of *al-Kashshāf* said: His saying ﴿and guidance and mercy﴾ is coordinated with the position of His saying ﴿that you may make clear﴾, except that they are in the accusative as objects of purpose (*mafʿūl lahu*), because they are the actions of Him who sent down the Book; and the *lām* entered upon His saying ﴿that you may make clear﴾ because it is the act of the addressee, not the act of the one who sent it down. Only that which is an act of that same agent can be in the accusative as an object of purpose.

The fourth issue: al-Kalbī said: the description of the Qur'an as being "guidance and mercy for a people who believe" does not negate that it is so for everyone, just as His saying at the beginning of Surat al-Baqarah: ﴿guidance for the God-conscious﴾ [al-Baqarah: 2] does not negate that it is guidance for all people, as He mentioned in His saying: ﴿a guidance for mankind and clear proofs of the guidance and the criterion﴾ [al-Baqarah: 185]. He specified the believers in the mention only because they accepted it and benefited from it, as in His saying: ﴿You are only a warner to those who fear it﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 45], because only this people benefited from his warning. And God knows best.

**Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 16, verses 65–67 (part 1 of 2):**

The Exalted said: ﴿And Allah sent down water from the sky, and with it gave life to the earth after its death. Indeed, in that is a sign for a people who listen.﴾ ﴿And indeed, in the livestock there is a lesson for you: We give you to drink from what is in their bellies, from between digested matter and blood, pure milk, palatable to the drinkers.﴾ ﴿And from the fruits of the date palms and the grapevines you take intoxicant and good provision. Indeed, in that is a sign for a people who reason.﴾

Know that we have mentioned that the greatest purpose of this mighty Qur'an is to establish four principles: the divine matters (al-Ilahiyyat, theology), prophethood (al-Nubuwwat), the return (al-Ma'ad, resurrection), and the affirmation of divine decree and destiny (al-Qada' wa'l-qadar). The greatest purpose among these four principles is to establish the divine matters. For this reason,

[Page 52]

whenever the discourse extends into a section concerning the threats against the disbelievers, it returns to establishing the divine matters. We have mentioned at the beginning of this surah that when He, the Exalted, intended to mention the proofs of the divine matters, He began with the celestial bodies, followed with the human being, made the third the animals, the fourth the plants, and the fifth the mention of the states of the sea and the land. Here in this verse, when He returned to establishing the proofs of the divine matters, He began first by mentioning the celestial things, saying: ﴿And Allah sent down water from the sky, and with it gave life to the earth after its death.﴾ The meaning is: He, the Exalted, created the sky in such a way that water descends from it, and that water becomes the cause of the earth's life. The intended meaning of the earth's life is the growth of crops, trees, blossoms and fruit after it had not been bearing fruit, and had not been beneficial. We have mentioned the establishment of these proofs many times.

Then He said: ﴿Indeed, in that is a sign for a people who listen﴾, listening with fairness and reflection, because whoever does not listen with his heart is as if he were deaf and did not listen.

The second type of proof mentioned in these verses is reasoning from the wondrous states of animals, and this is His saying: ﴿And indeed, in the livestock there is a lesson for you: We give you to drink from what is in their bellies﴾. We have already explained the meaning of "lesson" (ibrah) in His saying: ﴿there is a lesson for people of insight﴾ [Al 'Imran: 13]. There are several issues here:

**The first issue:** Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr, Hafs from 'Asim, Hamza and al-Kisa'i read ﴿nusqikum﴾ with a ḍamma on the nun (nusqīkum), while the rest read it with a fatḥa (naslaqīkum, i.e., nasqīkum with fatḥa). As for the one who reads it with a fatḥa on the nun, his argument is clear: you say "saqaytuhu" (I gave him to drink) until he is satisfied, and "asqīhi" (I give him to drink). Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And their Lord gave them to drink a pure drink﴾ [al-Insan: 21], and He said: ﴿And it is He who feeds me and gives me to drink﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 79], and He said: ﴿And they are given boiling water to drink﴾ [Muhammad: 15]. As for the one who reads it with a ḍamma on the nun, it is from your saying "asqāhu," when one makes a drink for him, as in His saying: ﴿And We gave you to drink sweet water﴾ [al-Mursalat: 27], and His saying: ﴿So We gave you to drink it﴾ [al-Hijr: 22]. The meaning here is: We made it, by its abundance and continuity, like giving drink. Abu 'Ubayd preferred the ḍamma and said: "Because it is continuous drinking, and what is most commonly said in this context is 'asqaytu'."

**The second issue:** His saying ﴿from what is in their bellies﴾. The pronoun refers back to the livestock (al-an'am), so the expected form would have been "from what is in their bellies" (feminine plural). The grammarians have given several explanations for this.

The first: the word al-an'am is singular in form but is used to indicate a plural group, like al-rahṭ, al-qawm, al-baqar and al-na'am. So, in terms of wording, it is a singular noun, and therefore its pronoun takes the singular form, which is the masculine. In terms of meaning, it is plural, and therefore its pronoun takes the plural form, which is the feminine. For this reason He said here ﴿fi buṭūnihi﴾ (in its bellies, masculine singular), and in Surat al-Mu'minun He said ﴿fi buṭūnihā﴾ (in their bellies, feminine plural) [al-Mu'minun: 21].

The second: His saying ﴿fi buṭūnihi﴾ means: in the bellies of what we have mentioned. This is the answer of al-Kisa'i. Al-Mubarrad said: "This is common in the Qur'an." He, the Exalted, said: ﴿So when he saw the sun rising, he said: This is my Lord﴾ [al-An'am: 78], meaning: this thing that is rising is my Lord. And He said: ﴿Indeed, it is a reminder, so whoever wills may remember it﴾ [Abasa: 11–12], meaning: remembers this thing.

Know that this is permissible only in cases where the feminine form is not a real feminine. As for the case where the feminine is real, it is not permissible. It is not correct in standard speech to say: "your female slave went" (jāriyatuka dhahaba) or "your male slave went away" (ghulāmuka dhahabat), supposing that we take it to refer to the soul (nasama).

The third: there is an ellipsis (idmar) here, and the implied meaning is: "We give you to drink from what is in their bellies the milk," since not all of them have milk.

**The third issue:** al-Farth is the dung (sirjin) of the rumen (karish). Al-Kalbi narrated from Abu Salih from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "When the fodder settles in the rumen, its lowest part becomes al-farth, its uppermost part becomes blood, and its middle part becomes milk. The blood flows in the veins and the milk flows in the udder, and the farth remains as it is. That is His saying: ﴿from between digested matter and blood, pure milk﴾, not mixed with blood or farth."

One may say: blood and milk are absolutely not produced in the rumen, and the evidence for this is sensory observation. These animals are slaughtered in succession, and no one has seen in their rumens either blood or milk. If the production of blood and milk took place in the rumen, it would have to be observed at some times. What observation has shown to be false cannot be adopted. Rather, the truth is that when an animal takes food, the fodder reaches its stomach if it is a human, or its rumen if it is one of the livestock or others. When it is cooked and the first digestion takes place in it, what is pure of it is drawn to the liver, and what is dense descends to the intestines. Then what results from it in the liver is cooked there and becomes blood, and that is the second digestion. This blood is mixed with yellow bile, black bile, and an increase of watery matter. As for yellow bile, it goes to the gall bladder, black bile to the spleen, and water to the kidney, and from there to the bladder. As for that blood, it enters the veins, which are the vessels growing from the liver, and there the third digestion takes place. Between the liver and the udder there are many vessels, so the blood pours into those vessels toward the udder. The udder is a soft, white, glandular flesh, and God, the Exalted, transforms the blood, at the moment of its flowing into that soft white glandular flesh, from the form of blood to the form of milk. This is the correct explanation of how milk is produced.

If it is said: these meanings are present in the male animal too, so why does milk not result from it?

We say: Divine wisdom required that everything be arranged in the proper manner that suits it and agrees with its benefit. The temperament of the male of every animal must be hot and dry, and the temperament of the female must be cold and moist. The wisdom in this is that the offspring forms inside the female's body, so the female must be specially endowed with abundant moisture for two reasons:

First: the offspring is formed from moisture, so the female's body must contain abundant moisture to become material for the formation of the offspring.

Second: when the offspring grows, the mother's body must be capable of expansion so that it can accommodate that offspring. When moisture predominates over the mother's body, her body becomes capable of expansion, and so it accommodates the offspring. Thus it has been established by what we have mentioned that He, the Exalted, specially endowed the female body of every animal with abundant moisture for this wisdom. Then the moisture that used to become material for the growth of the fetus while it was in the mother's womb, upon the separation of the fetus, pours into the breast and udder to become material for the nourishment of that little child.

Having understood this, know that the cause for which milk is produced from blood in the female is not present in the male, and so the difference has become clear.

Having understood this description, we say: the commentators said: what is meant by His saying ﴿from between digested matter and blood﴾ is that these three are produced in one place: the digested matter is at the bottom of the rumen, the blood is at its top, and the milk is in the middle. We have shown that this view is contrary to sense perception and experience, and also because if blood were produced at the top of the stomach and rumen, then whenever one vomited, one would have to vomit blood, and that is absolutely false. As for us, we say: what is meant by the verse is that milk is only produced from some parts of the blood, and blood is only produced from the subtle parts found in the digested matter, namely the edible things present in the rumen. This milk is produced from parts that were initially present among the digested matter, then were present among the blood a second time. So God, the Exalted, purified it from those dense, coarse parts, and created in it the attributes by which it becomes milk suitable for the body of the infant.

This is what we have achieved in this discussion, and Allah knows best.

* * *

**The fourth issue:** Know that the occurrence of milk in the breast, and its possession of the attributes by which it becomes suitable for nourishing the child, comprises wondrous wisdoms and marvelous secrets, which clear reason bears witness cannot be achieved except by the arrangement of the Wise Creator and the Merciful Governor. Its explanation is in several aspects.

**First:** He, the Exalted, created at the bottom of the stomach an outlet from which the heaviness of food exits. When a person takes food or a thin drink, that outlet closes completely, so that nothing of that food and drink exits until its digestion in the stomach is complete, and what is pure of it is drawn to the liver, while the heaviness remains there. Then that outlet opens and that heaviness is released from it. This is among the wonders that cannot occur except through the arrangement of the Wise Creator, because whenever the need for the food to remain in the stomach exists, that outlet closes; and when the need arises for that body to leave the stomach, it opens. The closing at one time and the opening at another, according to need and the calculation of benefit, cannot be accomplished except by the design of the Wise Creator.

**Second:** He, the Exalted, deposited in the liver a power that draws the subtle parts found in that food or drink, and does not draw the dense parts. And He created in the intestines a power that draws those dense parts, which are the heaviness, and does not draw the subtle parts at all. Had the matter been the reverse, the interest of the body would have been disrupted and this arrangement would have fallen into disorder.

**Third:** He, the Exalted, deposited in the liver a digestive, cooking power, so that those subtle parts are cooked in the liver and turn into blood. Then He deposited in the gall bladder a power that attracts yellow bile, in the spleen a power that attracts black bile, and in the kidney a power that attracts the excess watery matter, so that the pure blood remains, which is suitable for nourishing the body. The specification of each of these organs with that power and property cannot be achieved except by the decree of the Wise, the All-Knowing.

**Fourth:** At the time when the fetus is in the mother's womb, a plentiful portion of that blood pours to it, until it becomes material for the growth of that child's organs and its increase. When that fetus is separated from the womb, that portion pours to the side of the breast so that milk is produced from it, which becomes nourishment for it. When the child grows older, that portion no longer pours either into the womb or into the breast, but pours into the whole body of the one being nourished. Thus the pouring of that blood at every time into a different organ, in a manner suited to benefit and wisdom, cannot be accomplished except by the arrangement of the Wise, Chooser Creator.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 16, verses 65–67 (part 2 of 2):

The fifth: When the milk is produced in the udder, God Most High creates in the nipple small openings and narrow pores, arranged so that when suckling or milking reaches that nipple, the milk is separated out through those narrow pores. Because those pores are extremely narrow, only what is in the utmost purity and fineness can come out. The dense parts cannot pass through those narrow outlets, so they remain inside. The wisdom in creating those small openings and narrow passages at the tip of the nipple is that it acts like a filter (mişfāh): whatever is fine comes out, and whatever is dense is retained inside and does not come out. By this means the milk becomes pure, suited to the body of the infant and palatable to those who drink it.

The sixth: God Most High inspired the infant to suckle. Whenever the mother places the nipple in the infant's mouth, the infant immediately begins to suckle. Had the Chooser, the Merciful Agent, not inspired that little child to this specific action, the benefit of the milk's creation in the breast would not have been achieved.

The seventh: We have shown that God created the milk only from the surplus of the blood, and created the blood from the fine parts of that (food). Then He created the milk from some parts of that blood. Within the milk there come to be three kinds of parts with opposing natures. What is in it of fat is hot and moist; what is in it of watery substance is cold and moist; and what is in it of cheesy substance is cold and dry. These natures were not present in that herb which the goat consumed. Thus it becomes clear that these bodies never cease to transform from one attribute to another and from one state to another, although some of them are not compatible with one another nor similar to one another. At this point it becomes evident that these states occur through the management of a Wise, Merciful Agent who arranges the affairs of this world in accordance with the interests of His servants. Glory be to Him, to whom all the atoms of the higher and lower worlds bear witness, to the perfection of His power, the utmost of His wisdom and His mercy. To Him belong creation and command; blessed is God, Lord of the worlds.

As for His words ﴿palatable to the drinkers﴾, its meaning is: flowing smoothly in their throats, delicious and wholesome. It is said: "sāgha al-sharāb fī al-ḥalq" (the drink went down the throat) and "asāghahu ṣāḥibuhu" (its owner made it go down easily). From this is His saying: ﴿and he can hardly swallow it﴾ [Ibrahim: 17].

* * *

Fifth issue: The people of verification (ahl al-taḥqīq) said: Reflecting on the origin of milk indicates the existence of the Creator who chooses, may He be glorified, and in the same way it indicates the possibility of resurrection and gathering. This is because this herb that the animal eats is produced from water and earth. The Creator of the world arranged it in one arrangement, and turned that clay into plant and herb. Then, when the animal eats it, He arranged another arrangement and turned that herb into blood. Then He arranged yet another arrangement and turned that blood into milk. Then He arranged another arrangement, and from that milk came the fat and the cheese. This indicates that He, Most High, is able to transform these bodies from one attribute to another, and from one state to another. If that is so, it is not impossible that He is also able to turn the parts of the bodies of the dead back to the attribute of life and intellect as they were before. Thus this consideration indicates, from this aspect, that resurrection and the Last Day are a possible matter, not an impossible one. And God knows best.

* * *

Then God Most High said: ﴿And from the fruits of the date palms and the grapes you take from them intoxicants and good provision﴾. Know that when God Most High mentioned some benefits of the animals in the previous verse, He mentioned in this verse some benefits of plants. On this there are several issues:

First issue: If it is asked: To what does His saying ﴿and from the fruits of the date palms and the grapes﴾ relate?

We say: It relates to an omitted element, its implied sense being: "and We give you to drink from the fruits of the date palms and the grapes," i.e., from their juice. It is omitted because "We give you to drink" mentioned before it indicates it. His saying ﴿you take from it intoxicants﴾ is an explanation and clarification of the nature of the giving to drink.

Second issue: Al-Wahidi said: "al-a'nāb" (the grapes) is coordinated with "al-thamarāt" (the fruits), not with "al-nakhīl" (the date palms), because the sense would otherwise become: "and from the fruits of the grapes," while the grape itself is a fruit, and it has no other fruit.

Third issue: Regarding the interpretation of sakar (intoxicant) there are several views:

The first: Sakar is khamr (wine). It is called by the verbal noun of sakira, sakaran and sakran, like rashida, rashadan and rashdan. As for good provision, it refers to everything else made from date palms and grapes, such as rubb (concentrated juice), vinegar, date syrup (dibs), dates and raisins.

If it is asked: Wine is forbidden, so how does God mention it in the context of blessing?

They answered in two ways:

The first: This surah is Meccan, and the prohibition of wine was revealed in Surat al-Ma'ida. So the revelation of this verse was at a time when wine was not yet forbidden.

The second: There is no need to posit this abrogation (naskh), because God mentioned the beneficial aspects of these things and addressed the polytheists with them, and wine was among their drinks, so it was a benefit for them. Moreover, God, in this verse, also indicates its prohibition, because He distinguished between it and good provision in the mention. Therefore sakar must not be good provision. There is no doubt that it is good in terms of desire, so it must be said that its being good is renounced according to the Law, and this is the case only when it is forbidden.

The second view: Sakar is nabidh (a drink made by cooking), which is the juice of grapes, raisins or dates when it is boiled until two-thirds of it has gone, then left until it becomes strong. Abu Hanifa, may God have mercy on him, held it lawful up to the point of intoxication. He argues that this verse shows that sakar is lawful, because God mentioned it in the context of blessing and favour, and a hadith shows that wine is forbidden. He, peace be upon him, said: "Wine is forbidden in itself" (al-khamr ḥarām li-‘aynihā). This requires that sakar be something other than wine, and whoever affirms this distinction says it is cooked nabidh.

The third view: Sakar is food. This was said by Abu 'Ubayda, and he argued for it with the poet's verse:

"You made the honour of the noble into sakar"

That is: you made their disgrace your food. Al-Zajjaj said: This resembles wine more than food. The meaning is that you made yourself become intoxicated by the honour of the noble. The sense is that he made his fervour for backbiting people and tearing apart their honour equivalent to drinking wine.

Know that when God Most High mentioned these aspects, which are proofs from one angle and an enumeration of great blessings from another, He said: ﴿Indeed, in that is a sign for a people who use reason﴾. The meaning is: whoever is rational knows by necessity that these conditions cannot be brought about except by God, glory be to Him and exalted, so he infers from their occurrence the existence of the God who is Powerful and Wise. And God knows best.

**Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 16, verses 65–67 (part 1 of 2):**

The Exalted said: ﴿And Allah sent down water from the sky, and with it gave life to the earth after its death. Indeed, in that is a sign for a people who listen.﴾ ﴿And indeed, in the livestock there is a lesson for you: We give you to drink from what is in their bellies, from between digested matter and blood, pure milk, palatable to the drinkers.﴾ ﴿And from the fruits of the date palms and the grapevines you take intoxicant and good provision. Indeed, in that is a sign for a people who reason.﴾

Know that we have mentioned that the greatest purpose of this mighty Qur'an is to establish four principles: the divine matters (al-Ilahiyyat, theology), prophethood (al-Nubuwwat), the return (al-Ma'ad, resurrection), and the affirmation of divine decree and destiny (al-Qada' wa'l-qadar). The greatest purpose among these four principles is to establish the divine matters. For this reason,

[Page 52]

whenever the discourse extends into a section concerning the threats against the disbelievers, it returns to establishing the divine matters. We have mentioned at the beginning of this surah that when He, the Exalted, intended to mention the proofs of the divine matters, He began with the celestial bodies, followed with the human being, made the third the animals, the fourth the plants, and the fifth the mention of the states of the sea and the land. Here in this verse, when He returned to establishing the proofs of the divine matters, He began first by mentioning the celestial things, saying: ﴿And Allah sent down water from the sky, and with it gave life to the earth after its death.﴾ The meaning is: He, the Exalted, created the sky in such a way that water descends from it, and that water becomes the cause of the earth's life. The intended meaning of the earth's life is the growth of crops, trees, blossoms and fruit after it had not been bearing fruit, and had not been beneficial. We have mentioned the establishment of these proofs many times.

Then He said: ﴿Indeed, in that is a sign for a people who listen﴾, listening with fairness and reflection, because whoever does not listen with his heart is as if he were deaf and did not listen.

The second type of proof mentioned in these verses is reasoning from the wondrous states of animals, and this is His saying: ﴿And indeed, in the livestock there is a lesson for you: We give you to drink from what is in their bellies﴾. We have already explained the meaning of "lesson" (ibrah) in His saying: ﴿there is a lesson for people of insight﴾ [Al 'Imran: 13]. There are several issues here:

**The first issue:** Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr, Hafs from 'Asim, Hamza and al-Kisa'i read ﴿nusqikum﴾ with a ḍamma on the nun (nusqīkum), while the rest read it with a fatḥa (naslaqīkum, i.e., nasqīkum with fatḥa). As for the one who reads it with a fatḥa on the nun, his argument is clear: you say "saqaytuhu" (I gave him to drink) until he is satisfied, and "asqīhi" (I give him to drink). Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And their Lord gave them to drink a pure drink﴾ [al-Insan: 21], and He said: ﴿And it is He who feeds me and gives me to drink﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 79], and He said: ﴿And they are given boiling water to drink﴾ [Muhammad: 15]. As for the one who reads it with a ḍamma on the nun, it is from your saying "asqāhu," when one makes a drink for him, as in His saying: ﴿And We gave you to drink sweet water﴾ [al-Mursalat: 27], and His saying: ﴿So We gave you to drink it﴾ [al-Hijr: 22]. The meaning here is: We made it, by its abundance and continuity, like giving drink. Abu 'Ubayd preferred the ḍamma and said: "Because it is continuous drinking, and what is most commonly said in this context is 'asqaytu'."

**The second issue:** His saying ﴿from what is in their bellies﴾. The pronoun refers back to the livestock (al-an'am), so the expected form would have been "from what is in their bellies" (feminine plural). The grammarians have given several explanations for this.

The first: the word al-an'am is singular in form but is used to indicate a plural group, like al-rahṭ, al-qawm, al-baqar and al-na'am. So, in terms of wording, it is a singular noun, and therefore its pronoun takes the singular form, which is the masculine. In terms of meaning, it is plural, and therefore its pronoun takes the plural form, which is the feminine. For this reason He said here ﴿fi buṭūnihi﴾ (in its bellies, masculine singular), and in Surat al-Mu'minun He said ﴿fi buṭūnihā﴾ (in their bellies, feminine plural) [al-Mu'minun: 21].

The second: His saying ﴿fi buṭūnihi﴾ means: in the bellies of what we have mentioned. This is the answer of al-Kisa'i. Al-Mubarrad said: "This is common in the Qur'an." He, the Exalted, said: ﴿So when he saw the sun rising, he said: This is my Lord﴾ [al-An'am: 78], meaning: this thing that is rising is my Lord. And He said: ﴿Indeed, it is a reminder, so whoever wills may remember it﴾ [Abasa: 11–12], meaning: remembers this thing.

Know that this is permissible only in cases where the feminine form is not a real feminine. As for the case where the feminine is real, it is not permissible. It is not correct in standard speech to say: "your female slave went" (jāriyatuka dhahaba) or "your male slave went away" (ghulāmuka dhahabat), supposing that we take it to refer to the soul (nasama).

The third: there is an ellipsis (idmar) here, and the implied meaning is: "We give you to drink from what is in their bellies the milk," since not all of them have milk.

**The third issue:** al-Farth is the dung (sirjin) of the rumen (karish). Al-Kalbi narrated from Abu Salih from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "When the fodder settles in the rumen, its lowest part becomes al-farth, its uppermost part becomes blood, and its middle part becomes milk. The blood flows in the veins and the milk flows in the udder, and the farth remains as it is. That is His saying: ﴿from between digested matter and blood, pure milk﴾, not mixed with blood or farth."

One may say: blood and milk are absolutely not produced in the rumen, and the evidence for this is sensory observation. These animals are slaughtered in succession, and no one has seen in their rumens either blood or milk. If the production of blood and milk took place in the rumen, it would have to be observed at some times. What observation has shown to be false cannot be adopted. Rather, the truth is that when an animal takes food, the fodder reaches its stomach if it is a human, or its rumen if it is one of the livestock or others. When it is cooked and the first digestion takes place in it, what is pure of it is drawn to the liver, and what is dense descends to the intestines. Then what results from it in the liver is cooked there and becomes blood, and that is the second digestion. This blood is mixed with yellow bile, black bile, and an increase of watery matter. As for yellow bile, it goes to the gall bladder, black bile to the spleen, and water to the kidney, and from there to the bladder. As for that blood, it enters the veins, which are the vessels growing from the liver, and there the third digestion takes place. Between the liver and the udder there are many vessels, so the blood pours into those vessels toward the udder. The udder is a soft, white, glandular flesh, and God, the Exalted, transforms the blood, at the moment of its flowing into that soft white glandular flesh, from the form of blood to the form of milk. This is the correct explanation of how milk is produced.

If it is said: these meanings are present in the male animal too, so why does milk not result from it?

We say: Divine wisdom required that everything be arranged in the proper manner that suits it and agrees with its benefit. The temperament of the male of every animal must be hot and dry, and the temperament of the female must be cold and moist. The wisdom in this is that the offspring forms inside the female's body, so the female must be specially endowed with abundant moisture for two reasons:

First: the offspring is formed from moisture, so the female's body must contain abundant moisture to become material for the formation of the offspring.

Second: when the offspring grows, the mother's body must be capable of expansion so that it can accommodate that offspring. When moisture predominates over the mother's body, her body becomes capable of expansion, and so it accommodates the offspring. Thus it has been established by what we have mentioned that He, the Exalted, specially endowed the female body of every animal with abundant moisture for this wisdom. Then the moisture that used to become material for the growth of the fetus while it was in the mother's womb, upon the separation of the fetus, pours into the breast and udder to become material for the nourishment of that little child.

Having understood this, know that the cause for which milk is produced from blood in the female is not present in the male, and so the difference has become clear.

Having understood this description, we say: the commentators said: what is meant by His saying ﴿from between digested matter and blood﴾ is that these three are produced in one place: the digested matter is at the bottom of the rumen, the blood is at its top, and the milk is in the middle. We have shown that this view is contrary to sense perception and experience, and also because if blood were produced at the top of the stomach and rumen, then whenever one vomited, one would have to vomit blood, and that is absolutely false. As for us, we say: what is meant by the verse is that milk is only produced from some parts of the blood, and blood is only produced from the subtle parts found in the digested matter, namely the edible things present in the rumen. This milk is produced from parts that were initially present among the digested matter, then were present among the blood a second time. So God, the Exalted, purified it from those dense, coarse parts, and created in it the attributes by which it becomes milk suitable for the body of the infant.

This is what we have achieved in this discussion, and Allah knows best.

* * *

**The fourth issue:** Know that the occurrence of milk in the breast, and its possession of the attributes by which it becomes suitable for nourishing the child, comprises wondrous wisdoms and marvelous secrets, which clear reason bears witness cannot be achieved except by the arrangement of the Wise Creator and the Merciful Governor. Its explanation is in several aspects.

**First:** He, the Exalted, created at the bottom of the stomach an outlet from which the heaviness of food exits. When a person takes food or a thin drink, that outlet closes completely, so that nothing of that food and drink exits until its digestion in the stomach is complete, and what is pure of it is drawn to the liver, while the heaviness remains there. Then that outlet opens and that heaviness is released from it. This is among the wonders that cannot occur except through the arrangement of the Wise Creator, because whenever the need for the food to remain in the stomach exists, that outlet closes; and when the need arises for that body to leave the stomach, it opens. The closing at one time and the opening at another, according to need and the calculation of benefit, cannot be accomplished except by the design of the Wise Creator.

**Second:** He, the Exalted, deposited in the liver a power that draws the subtle parts found in that food or drink, and does not draw the dense parts. And He created in the intestines a power that draws those dense parts, which are the heaviness, and does not draw the subtle parts at all. Had the matter been the reverse, the interest of the body would have been disrupted and this arrangement would have fallen into disorder.

**Third:** He, the Exalted, deposited in the liver a digestive, cooking power, so that those subtle parts are cooked in the liver and turn into blood. Then He deposited in the gall bladder a power that attracts yellow bile, in the spleen a power that attracts black bile, and in the kidney a power that attracts the excess watery matter, so that the pure blood remains, which is suitable for nourishing the body. The specification of each of these organs with that power and property cannot be achieved except by the decree of the Wise, the All-Knowing.

**Fourth:** At the time when the fetus is in the mother's womb, a plentiful portion of that blood pours to it, until it becomes material for the growth of that child's organs and its increase. When that fetus is separated from the womb, that portion pours to the side of the breast so that milk is produced from it, which becomes nourishment for it. When the child grows older, that portion no longer pours either into the womb or into the breast, but pours into the whole body of the one being nourished. Thus the pouring of that blood at every time into a different organ, in a manner suited to benefit and wisdom, cannot be accomplished except by the arrangement of the Wise, Chooser Creator.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 16, verses 65–67 (part 2 of 2):

The fifth: When the milk is produced in the udder, God Most High creates in the nipple small openings and narrow pores, arranged so that when suckling or milking reaches that nipple, the milk is separated out through those narrow pores. Because those pores are extremely narrow, only what is in the utmost purity and fineness can come out. The dense parts cannot pass through those narrow outlets, so they remain inside. The wisdom in creating those small openings and narrow passages at the tip of the nipple is that it acts like a filter (mişfāh): whatever is fine comes out, and whatever is dense is retained inside and does not come out. By this means the milk becomes pure, suited to the body of the infant and palatable to those who drink it.

The sixth: God Most High inspired the infant to suckle. Whenever the mother places the nipple in the infant's mouth, the infant immediately begins to suckle. Had the Chooser, the Merciful Agent, not inspired that little child to this specific action, the benefit of the milk's creation in the breast would not have been achieved.

The seventh: We have shown that God created the milk only from the surplus of the blood, and created the blood from the fine parts of that (food). Then He created the milk from some parts of that blood. Within the milk there come to be three kinds of parts with opposing natures. What is in it of fat is hot and moist; what is in it of watery substance is cold and moist; and what is in it of cheesy substance is cold and dry. These natures were not present in that herb which the goat consumed. Thus it becomes clear that these bodies never cease to transform from one attribute to another and from one state to another, although some of them are not compatible with one another nor similar to one another. At this point it becomes evident that these states occur through the management of a Wise, Merciful Agent who arranges the affairs of this world in accordance with the interests of His servants. Glory be to Him, to whom all the atoms of the higher and lower worlds bear witness, to the perfection of His power, the utmost of His wisdom and His mercy. To Him belong creation and command; blessed is God, Lord of the worlds.

As for His words ﴿palatable to the drinkers﴾, its meaning is: flowing smoothly in their throats, delicious and wholesome. It is said: "sāgha al-sharāb fī al-ḥalq" (the drink went down the throat) and "asāghahu ṣāḥibuhu" (its owner made it go down easily). From this is His saying: ﴿and he can hardly swallow it﴾ [Ibrahim: 17].

Fifth issue: The people of verification (ahl al-taḥqīq) said: Reflecting on the origin of milk indicates the existence of the Creator who chooses, may He be glorified, and in the same way it indicates the possibility of resurrection and gathering. Then He arranged another arrangement, and from that milk came the fat and the cheese. This indicates that He, Most High, is able to transform these bodies from one attribute to another, and from one state to another. If that is so, it is not impossible that He is also able to turn the parts of the bodies of the dead back to the attribute of life and intellect as they were before. Thus this consideration indicates, from this aspect, that resurrection and the Last Day are a possible matter, not an impossible one. And God knows best.

Then what results from it in the liver is cooked there and becomes blood, and that is the second digestion. This blood is mixed with yellow bile, black bile, and an increase of watery matter. As for yellow bile, it goes to the gall bladder, black bile to the spleen, and water to the kidney, and from there to the bladder. As for that blood, it enters the veins, which are the vessels growing from the liver, and there the third digestion takes place. Between the liver and the udder there are many vessels, so the blood pours into those vessels toward the udder. The udder is a soft, white, glandular flesh, and God, the Exalted, transforms the blood, at the moment of its flowing into that soft white glandular flesh, from the form of blood to the form of milk. This is the correct explanation of how milk is produced.

If it is said: these meanings are present in the male animal too, so why does milk not result from it?

We say: Divine wisdom required that everything be arranged in the proper manner that suits it and agrees with its benefit. The temperament of the male of every animal must be hot and dry, and the temperament of the female must be cold and moist. The wisdom in this is that the offspring forms inside the female's body, so the female must be specially endowed with abundant moisture for two reasons:

First: the offspring is formed from moisture, so the female's body must contain abundant moisture to become material for the formation of the offspring.

Second: when the offspring grows, the mother's body must be capable of expansion so that it can accommodate that offspring. When moisture predominates over the mother's body, her body becomes capable of expansion, and so it accommodates the offspring. Thus it has been established by what we have mentioned that He, the Exalted, specially endowed the female body of every animal with abundant moisture for this wisdom. Then the moisture that used to become material for the growth of the fetus while it was in the mother's womb, upon the separation of the fetus, pours into the breast and udder to become material for the nourishment of that little child.

Having understood this, know that the cause for which milk is produced from blood in the female is not present in the male, and so the difference has become clear.

Having understood this description, we say: the commentators said: what is meant by His saying ﴿from between digested matter and blood﴾ is that these three are produced in one place: the digested matter is at the bottom of the rumen, the blood is at its top, and the milk is in the middle. We have shown that this view is contrary to sense perception and experience, and also because if blood were produced at the top of the stomach and rumen, then whenever one vomited, one would have to vomit blood, and that is absolutely false. As for us, we say: what is meant by the verse is that milk is only produced from some parts of the blood, and blood is only produced from the subtle parts found in the digested matter, namely the edible things present in the rumen. This milk is produced from parts that were initially present among the digested matter, then were present among the blood a second time. So God, the Exalted, purified it from those dense, coarse parts, and created in it the attributes by which it becomes milk suitable for the body of the infant.

This is what we have achieved in this discussion, and Allah knows best.

* * *

**The fourth issue:** Know that the occurrence of milk in the breast, and its possession of the attributes by which it becomes suitable for nourishing the child, comprises wondrous wisdoms and marvelous secrets, which clear reason bears witness cannot be achieved except by the arrangement of the Wise Creator and the Merciful Governor. Its explanation is in several aspects.

**First:** He, the Exalted, created at the bottom of the stomach an outlet from which the heaviness of food exits. When a person takes food or a thin drink, that outlet closes completely, so that nothing of that food and drink exits until its digestion in the stomach is complete, and what is pure of it is drawn to the liver, while the heaviness remains there. Then that outlet opens and that heaviness is released from it. This is among the wonders that cannot occur except through the arrangement of the Wise Creator, because whenever the need for the food to remain in the stomach exists, that outlet closes; and when the need arises for that body to leave the stomach, it opens. The closing at one time and the opening at another, according to need and the calculation of benefit, cannot be accomplished except by the design of the Wise Creator.

**Second:** He, the Exalted, deposited in the liver a power that draws the subtle parts found in that food or drink, and does not draw the dense parts. And He created in the intestines a power that draws those dense parts, which are the heaviness, and does not draw the subtle parts at all. Had the matter been the reverse, the interest of the body would have been disrupted and this arrangement would have fallen into disorder.

**Third:** He, the Exalted, deposited in the liver a digestive, cooking power, so that those subtle parts are cooked in the liver and turn into blood. Then He deposited in the gall bladder a power that attracts yellow bile, in the spleen a power that attracts black bile, and in the kidney a power that attracts the excess watery matter, so that the pure blood remains, which is suitable for nourishing the body. The specification of each of these organs with that power and property cannot be achieved except by the decree of the Wise, the All-Knowing.

**Fourth:** At the time when the fetus is in the mother's womb, a plentiful portion of that blood pours to it, until it becomes material for the growth of that child's organs and its increase. When that fetus is separated from the womb, that portion pours to the side of the breast so that milk is produced from it, which becomes nourishment for it. When the child grows older, that portion no longer pours either into the womb or into the breast, but pours into the whole body of the one being nourished. Thus the pouring of that blood at every time into a different organ, in a manner suited to benefit and wisdom, cannot be accomplished except by the arrangement of the Wise, Chooser Creator.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 16, verses 65–67 (part 2 of 2):

The fifth: When the milk is produced in the udder, God Most High creates in the nipple small openings and narrow pores, arranged so that when suckling or milking reaches that nipple, the milk is separated out through those narrow pores. Because those pores are extremely narrow, only what is in the utmost purity and fineness can come out. The dense parts cannot pass through those narrow outlets, so they remain inside. The wisdom in creating those small openings and narrow passages at the tip of the nipple is that it acts like a filter (mişfāh): whatever is fine comes out, and whatever is dense is retained inside and does not come out. By this means the milk becomes pure, suited to the body of the infant and palatable to those who drink it.

The sixth: God Most High inspired the infant to suckle. Whenever the mother places the nipple in the infant's mouth, the infant immediately begins to suckle. Had the Chooser, the Merciful Agent, not inspired that little child to this specific action, the benefit of the milk's creation in the breast would not have been achieved.

The seventh: We have shown that God created the milk only from the surplus of the blood, and created the blood from the fine parts of that (food). Then He created the milk from some parts of that blood. Within the milk there come to be three kinds of parts with opposing natures. What is in it of fat is hot and moist; what is in it of watery substance is cold and moist; and what is in it of cheesy substance is cold and dry. These natures were not present in that herb which the goat consumed. Thus it becomes clear that these bodies never cease to transform from one attribute to another and from one state to another, although some of them are not compatible with one another nor similar to one another. At this point it becomes evident that these states occur through the management of a Wise, Merciful Agent who arranges the affairs of this world in accordance with the interests of His servants. Glory be to Him, to whom all the atoms of the higher and lower worlds bear witness, to the perfection of His power, the utmost of His wisdom and His mercy. To Him belong creation and command; blessed is God, Lord of the worlds.

As for His words ﴿palatable to the drinkers﴾, its meaning is: flowing smoothly in their throats, delicious and wholesome. It is said: "sāgha al-sharāb fī al-ḥalq" (the drink went down the throat) and "asāghahu ṣāḥibuhu" (its owner made it go down easily). From this is His saying: ﴿and he can hardly swallow it﴾ [Ibrahim: 17].

* * *

Fifth issue: The people of verification (ahl al-taḥqīq) said: Reflecting on the origin of milk indicates the existence of the Creator who chooses, may He be glorified, and in the same way it indicates the possibility of resurrection and gathering. This is because this herb that the animal eats is produced from water and earth. The Creator of the world arranged it in one arrangement, and turned that clay into plant and herb. Then, when the animal eats it, He arranged another arrangement and turned that herb into blood. Then He arranged yet another arrangement and turned that blood into milk. Then He arranged another arrangement, and from that milk came the fat and the cheese. This indicates that He, Most High, is able to transform these bodies from one attribute to another, and from one state to another. If that is so, it is not impossible that He is also able to turn the parts of the bodies of the dead back to the attribute of life and intellect as they were before. Thus this consideration indicates, from this aspect, that resurrection and the Last Day are a possible matter, not an impossible one. And God knows best.

* * *

Then God Most High said: ﴿And from the fruits of the date palms and the grapes you take from them intoxicants and good provision﴾. Know that when God Most High mentioned some benefits of the animals in the previous verse, He mentioned in this verse some benefits of plants. On this there are several issues:

First issue: If it is asked: To what does His saying ﴿and from the fruits of the date palms and the grapes﴾ relate?

We say: It relates to an omitted element, its implied sense being: "and We give you to drink from the fruits of the date palms and the grapes," i.e., from their juice. It is omitted because "We give you to drink" mentioned before it indicates it. His saying ﴿you take from it intoxicants﴾ is an explanation and clarification of the nature of the giving to drink.

Second issue: Al-Wahidi said: "al-a'nāb" (the grapes) is coordinated with "al-thamarāt" (the fruits), not with "al-nakhīl" (the date palms), because the sense would otherwise become: "and from the fruits of the grapes," while the grape itself is a fruit, and it has no other fruit.

Third issue: Regarding the interpretation of sakar (intoxicant) there are several views:

The first: Sakar is khamr (wine). It is called by the verbal noun of sakira, sakaran and sakran, like rashida, rashadan and rashdan. As for good provision, it refers to everything else made from date palms and grapes, such as rubb (concentrated juice), vinegar, date syrup (dibs), dates and raisins.

If it is asked: Wine is forbidden, so how does God mention it in the context of blessing?

They answered in two ways:

The first: This surah is Meccan, and the prohibition of wine was revealed in Surat al-Ma'ida. So the revelation of this verse was at a time when wine was not yet forbidden.

The second: There is no need to posit this abrogation (naskh), because God mentioned the beneficial aspects of these things and addressed the polytheists with them, and wine was among their drinks, so it was a benefit for them. Moreover, God, in this verse, also indicates its prohibition, because He distinguished between it and good provision in the mention. Therefore sakar must not be good provision. There is no doubt that it is good in terms of desire, so it must be said that its being good is renounced according to the Law, and this is the case only when it is forbidden.

The second view: Sakar is nabidh (a drink made by cooking), which is the juice of grapes, raisins or dates when it is boiled until two-thirds of it has gone, then left until it becomes strong. Abu Hanifa, may God have mercy on him, held it lawful up to the point of intoxication. He argues that this verse shows that sakar is lawful, because God mentioned it in the context of blessing and favour, and a hadith shows that wine is forbidden. He, peace be upon him, said: "Wine is forbidden in itself" (al-khamr ḥarām li-‘aynihā). This requires that sakar be something other than wine, and whoever affirms this distinction says it is cooked nabidh.

The third view: Sakar is food. This was said by Abu 'Ubayda, and he argued for it with the poet's verse:

"You made the honour of the noble into sakar"

That is: you made their disgrace your food. Al-Zajjaj said: This resembles wine more than food. The meaning is that you made yourself become intoxicated by the honour of the noble. The sense is that he made his fervour for backbiting people and tearing apart their honour equivalent to drinking wine.

Know that when God Most High mentioned these aspects, which are proofs from one angle and an enumeration of great blessings from another, He said: ﴿Indeed, in that is a sign for a people who use reason﴾. The meaning is: whoever is rational knows by necessity that these conditions cannot be brought about except by God, glory be to Him and exalted, so he infers from their occurrence the existence of the God who is Powerful and Wise. And God knows best.
