Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 16, verses 68–69 (part 1 of 2):

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And your Lord revealed to the bee: "Take for yourself dwellings in the mountains, and in the trees, and in what they erect."﴾ ﴿Then eat from all the fruits and follow the ways of your Lord, submissively. There emerges from their bellies a drink, varying in its colours, in which is healing for mankind. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who give thought.﴾

Know that when He, exalted is He, explained that the extraction of milk from livestock, and the extraction of intoxicant and good provision from the fruits of the date palms and grapevines, are compelling proofs and dazzling clear signs that this world has a God who is powerful, choosing and wise, then likewise the extraction of honey from the bee is a decisive proof and a shining demonstration of establishing this aim. In the verse there are several issues:

The first issue: His saying, ﴿And your Lord revealed to the bee.﴾ It is said: waḥā and awḥā, and it means inspiration (ilhām). What is meant by inspiration is that He, exalted is He, established within their natures these wondrous works which wise humans are unable to perform. Its explanation is in several aspects:

The first: they build hexagonal dwellings from equal sides, none of which exceeds another merely by their nature, and wise humans cannot build such dwellings except with instruments and tools such as the ruler and the compass.

The second: it has been established in geometry that if those dwellings were shaped in forms other than hexagons, there would necessarily remain between those dwellings empty, wasted gaps.

Page 57

But when those dwellings are hexagonal, no wasted gaps remain between them. So the guiding of that weak creature to this subtle, precise and delicate wisdom is among the marvels.

The third: among them there arises one that is like a chief over the rest. That one is greater in body than the others, its command is executed over the rest, and they serve it and carry it when it flies. This too is among the marvels.

The fourth: when they migrate from their hive, they go together with the collective to another place. When they wish to return them to their hive, they strike the tanbur (lute) and musical instruments, and through those melodies they are able to return them to their hive. This too is a wondrous state. Since this creature is distinguished by these wondrous properties, which indicate great intelligence and shrewdness, and since the acquisition of these kinds of shrewdness is only by way of inspiration, which is a state akin to revelation, He, exalted is He, said concerning it: ﴿And your Lord revealed to the bee.﴾

Know that revelation (waḥy) has been used concerning the prophets, by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It is not for a human that Allah should speak to him except by revelation﴾ [al-Shura: 51]; and concerning the saints (awliya') He also said: ﴿And when I revealed to the disciples﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 111]; and in the sense of inspiration concerning humans He said: ﴿And We revealed to the mother of Moses﴾ [al-Qasas: 7]; and concerning the rest of the animals, as in His saying: ﴿And your Lord revealed to the bee.﴾ Each of these categories has a particular meaning. And Allah knows best.

The second issue: al-Zajjaj said: it is permissible to say that this creature was named naḥl (bee) because Allah bestowed (naḥala) upon people the honey that emerges from their bellies. Others said: naḥl is masculine and feminine, and it is feminine in the dialect of the Hijaz, and for this reason Allah made it feminine; likewise every collective noun whose singular differs from it only by the ta' marbuṭa.

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿that take for yourself dwellings in the mountains, and in the trees, and in what they erect.﴾ Concerning this there are issues:

The first issue: the author of al-Kashshaf said: ﴿an ittakhidhi﴾ is the explanatory "an", because revelation contains the sense of saying. It was read: (biyūtan) with a kasra on the bā'. ﴿And in the trees and in what they erect﴾ means: what they build and roof. In it there are two dialects in which it was recited: with a ḍamma on the rā' and with a kasra, like yaʿkufūna and yaʿkifūna.

Know that bees are of two kinds:

The first kind: those that dwell in the mountains and thickets, and no one among people tends them.

The second kind: those that dwell in people's houses and are under people's care. The first is what is meant by His saying: ﴿that take for yourself dwellings in the mountains, and in the trees.﴾

The second is what is meant by His saying: ﴿and in what they erect,﴾ which is the bee-hives.

If it is asked: what is the meaning of "min" in His saying: ﴿that take for yourself dwellings in the mountains, and in the trees, and in what they erect﴾, and why was it not said "in the mountains and in the trees"?

We say: it is intended to convey the sense of partitiveness, and that they should not build their dwellings on every mountain and every tree, but in dwellings that suit their interests and befit them.

The second issue: the apparent meaning of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿that take for yourself dwellings in the mountains﴾ is a command, and they have differed concerning it. Some people say: it is not far-fetched that these animals have intellects, and it is not far-fetched that a command and prohibition from Allah, exalted is He, be directed at them. Others said: it is not so, rather what is meant by it is that He, exalted is He, created within them instincts and natures which necessitate these conditions. The thorough discussion of this issue is mentioned in the explanation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O ants, enter your dwellings﴾ [al-Naml: 18].

Page 58

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Then eat from all the fruits﴾. The word "min" here is either partitive or denotes the beginning of the limit. I have seen in the books of medicine that He, exalted is He, arranged this world in a certain way: that in the nights a subtle dew arises in the air, and that dew falls upon the leaves of trees. Those dewy particles may be tiny and subtle, scattered over the leaves and flowers, and they may be numerous such that perceptible parts gather from them.

As for the second kind, it is like terengabin (manna), which is a dew that descends from the air and gathers on the tips of the tamarisk in some lands, and that is perceptible.

As for the first kind, it is that which Allah, exalted is He, inspired in this bee, so that it gathers those particles from the flowers and the leaves of trees with its mouths, eats them and nourishes itself with them. When it is satiated, it gathers again with its mouths some of those parts and carries them to its dwellings and places them there, because it strives to store its nourishment for itself. When a large quantity of those dewy parts has gathered in its dwellings, that is honey. Some people say that the bee eats from the good flowers and fragrant leaves certain things, and then He, exalted is He, transforms those substances within its body into honey, and then it vomits again, and that is honey. The first view is closer to reason and more consistent with induction, for the nature of terengabin is close to honey in taste and form, and there is no doubt that it is a dew which arises in the air and falls upon the tips of trees and flowers, so likewise here. Furthermore, we observe that this bee feeds only on honey, and for this reason, when we extract honey from the bee-hives we leave for them a remainder of it so that they may feed on it. So we know that they feed only on honey, and that they settle on trees and flowers only because they feed on those dewy honeyed parts falling from the air upon them.

Having known this, we say: His saying, ﴿Then eat from all the fruits﴾, the word "min" here is for the beginning of the limit, and on this view it is not partitive.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿then follow the ways of your Lord﴾. The meaning is: then eat every fruit you desire, and when you have eaten it, follow the ways of your Lord in the paths He inspired and made you understand for the making of honey; or the meaning is: follow, in seeking those fruits, the ways of your Lord. As for His saying: ﴿submissively﴾, there are two views.

The first: it is a state (ḥāl) of "the ways", because Allah made them submissive, facilitated and eased them for it, as in His saying: ﴿He is the One who made the earth docile for you﴾ [al-Mulk: 15].

The second: it is a state of the pronoun in ﴿follow﴾, meaning: and you, O bee, are submissive, compliant with what you have been commanded, not refusing.

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿There emerges from their bellies﴾, and concerning this there are two discussions:

The first discussion: this is a shift from address to the third person, and the reason for it is that the purpose of mentioning these conditions is that the responsible human being should argue, by them, for the power, wisdom and good management of Allah concerning the conditions of the upper and lower worlds. It is as if He, exalted is He, when He addressed the bee with what has been mentioned, addressed the human and said: We inspired this bee with these marvels, so that there might emerge from their bellies a drink varying in its colours.

The second discussion: we have mentioned that some people say that honey is an expression for particles of dew that arise in the air and fall

Page 59

upon the tips of trees and upon the leaves and flowers, and the wasp picks them up with its mouth. If we take this view, then what is meant by His saying: ﴿There emerges from their bellies﴾ is: from their mouths, and every cavity inside the body is called a belly ("baṭn"). Do you not see that they say: "the bellies of the brain" (buṭūn al-dimāgh), meaning its cavities? So likewise here: there emerges from their bellies, that is, from their mouths. As for the view of the literalists, namely that the bee eats the leaves and fruits and then vomits, and that this is honey, the statement is clear.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿a drink, varying in its colours, in which is healing for mankind﴾. Know that He, exalted is He, described honey by these three attributes:

The first attribute: that it is a drink, and the matter is so, for it is sometimes drunk alone and sometimes made into beverages.

The second attribute: His saying: ﴿varying in its colours﴾, meaning: that among it is red, white and yellow. A parallel to this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And among the mountains are streaks, white and red, varying in their colours, and deep black﴾ [Fatir: 27]. The purpose of it is to refute the claim of nature, for this substance, though of uniform nature, came into being in varying colours, which shows that the occurrence of those colours is by the arrangement of a choosing agent, not for the sake of the creation of nature.

The third attribute: His saying: ﴿in which is healing for mankind﴾, and concerning it there are two views:

The first view, which is the correct one, is that it is an attribute of honey.

If they say: how can it be healing for people when it harms in cases of yellow bile and aggravates bitterness?

We say: He, exalted is He, did not say that it is a healing for all people, for every disease and in every condition. Rather, since it is a healing for some people with some ailments, it is fitting to describe it as having healing in it. What shows that it is a healing in general is that hardly any electuary (ma'jūn) is made whose completion and perfection is not achieved by kneading with honey, and also the beverages made from it are very beneficial in phlegmatic diseases.

The second view, which is the view of Mujahid, is that what is meant is: the Qur'an is a healing for mankind. On this interpretation, the account of the production of honey from the bee ends at His saying: ﴿There emerges from their bellies a drink varying in its colours﴾; then He begins and says: ﴿in it is healing for mankind﴾, meaning: in this Qur'an there has come about what is a healing for mankind from disbelief and innovation, like that which is in the story of the bee. It is reported from Ibn Mas'ud that honey is a healing from every disease, and the Qur'an is a healing for what is in the breasts.

Know that this view is weak, and two things indicate it:

The first: the pronoun in His saying: ﴿in it is healing for mankind﴾ must refer to the nearest of what has been mentioned, and that is nothing other than His saying: ﴿a drink varying in its colours﴾. As for ruling that this pronoun refers to the Qur'an, although it has not been mentioned previously, that is not appropriate.

The second: what Abu Sa'id al-Khudri narrated: that a man came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "My brother complains of his stomach." He said: "Give him honey to drink." He went and then returned and said: "I gave him to drink, but it did not avail him anything." He, peace be upon him, said: "Go and give him honey to drink." He went and gave him to drink, and it was as if he had been released from a shackle. He said: "Allah has spoken the truth and your brother's belly has lied." They understood His saying: "Allah has spoken the truth and your brother's belly has lied" as referring to His saying: ﴿in it is healing for mankind﴾, and that is only valid if this is an attribute of honey.

If someone says: what is meant by his saying, peace be upon him: "Allah has spoken the truth and your brother's belly has lied"?

Page 60

We say: perhaps he, peace be upon him, knew through the light of revelation that the benefit of that honey would appear later. Since its benefit did not appear at the time, although he, peace be upon him, knew that it would appear later, this was like a lie, and for this reason the term was applied to it.

Then God concluded the verse with His saying: ﴿Indeed in that is a sign for a people who give thought.﴾ Know that the explanation of this verse is from several aspects:

The first: the bee's specialization in those subtle sciences and obscure knowledge, such as building hexagonal hives and the other conditions we have mentioned.

The second: its guidance to all those honey-producing parts from the tips of trees and leaves.

The third: God's creation of the beneficial particles in the atmosphere of the air, then their being cast onto the tips of trees and leaves, then the inspiring of the bee to gather them after they have been scattered. All of this is wondrous, indicating that the God of the world built its arrangement upon regard for wisdom and benefit. And God knows best.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿that take for yourself dwellings in the mountains, and in the trees, and in what they erect.﴾ Concerning this there are issues:

The first issue: the author of al-Kashshaf said: ﴿an ittakhidhi﴾ is the explanatory "an", because revelation contains the sense of saying. It was read: (biyūtan) with a kasra on the bā'. ﴿And in the trees and in what they erect﴾ means: what they build and roof. In it there are two dialects in which it was recited: with a ḍamma on the rā' and with a kasra, like yaʿkufūna and yaʿkifūna.

Know that bees are of two kinds:

The first kind: those that dwell in the mountains and thickets, and no one among people tends them.

The second kind: those that dwell in people's houses and are under people's care. The first is what is meant by His saying: ﴿that take for yourself dwellings in the mountains, and in the trees.﴾

The second is what is meant by His saying: ﴿and in what they erect,﴾ which is the bee-hives.

If it is asked: what is the meaning of "min" in His saying: ﴿that take for yourself dwellings in the mountains, and in the trees, and in what they erect﴾, and why was it not said "in the mountains and in the trees"?

We say: it is intended to convey the sense of partitiveness, and that they should not build their dwellings on every mountain and every tree, but in dwellings that suit their interests and befit them.

The second issue: the apparent meaning of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿that take for yourself dwellings in the mountains﴾ is a command, and they have differed concerning it. Some people say: it is not far-fetched that these animals have intellects, and it is not far-fetched that a command and prohibition from Allah, exalted is He, be directed at them. Others said: it is not so, rather what is meant by it is that He, exalted is He, created within them instincts and natures which necessitate these conditions. The thorough discussion of this issue is mentioned in the explanation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O ants, enter your dwellings﴾ [al-Naml: 18].

Page 58

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Then eat from all the fruits﴾. The word "min" here is either partitive or denotes the beginning of the limit. I have seen in the books of medicine that He, exalted is He, arranged this world in a certain way: that in the nights a subtle dew arises in the air, and that dew falls upon the leaves of trees. Those dewy particles may be tiny and subtle, scattered over the leaves and flowers, and they may be numerous such that perceptible parts gather from them.

As for the second kind, it is like terengabin (manna), which is a dew that descends from the air and gathers on the tips of the tamarisk in some lands, and that is perceptible.

As for the first kind, it is that which Allah, exalted is He, inspired in this bee, so that it gathers those particles from the flowers and the leaves of trees with its mouths, eats them and nourishes itself with them. When it is satiated, it gathers again with its mouths some of those parts and carries them to its dwellings and places them there, because it strives to store its nourishment for itself. When a large quantity of those dewy parts has gathered in its dwellings, that is honey. Some people say that the bee eats from the good flowers and fragrant leaves certain things, and then He, exalted is He, transforms those substances within its body into honey, and then it vomits again, and that is honey. The first view is closer to reason and more consistent with induction, for the nature of terengabin is close to honey in taste and form, and there is no doubt that it is a dew which arises in the air and falls upon the tips of trees and flowers, so likewise here. Furthermore, we observe that this bee feeds only on honey, and for this reason, when we extract honey from the bee-hives we leave for them a remainder of it so that they may feed on it. So we know that they feed only on honey, and that they settle on trees and flowers only because they feed on those dewy honeyed parts falling from the air upon them.

Having known this, we say: His saying, ﴿Then eat from all the fruits﴾, the word "min" here is for the beginning of the limit, and on this view it is not partitive.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿then follow the ways of your Lord﴾. The meaning is: then eat every fruit you desire, and when you have eaten it, follow the ways of your Lord in the paths He inspired and made you understand for the making of honey; or the meaning is: follow, in seeking those fruits, the ways of your Lord. As for His saying: ﴿submissively﴾, there are two views.

The first: it is a state (ḥāl) of "the ways", because Allah made them submissive, facilitated and eased them for it, as in His saying: ﴿He is the One who made the earth docile for you﴾ [al-Mulk: 15].

The second: it is a state of the pronoun in ﴿follow﴾, meaning: and you, O bee, are submissive, compliant with what you have been commanded, not refusing.

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿There emerges from their bellies﴾, and concerning this there are two discussions:

The first discussion: this is a shift from address to the third person, and the reason for it is that the purpose of mentioning these conditions is that the responsible human being should argue, by them, for the power, wisdom and good management of Allah concerning the conditions of the upper and lower worlds. It is as if He, exalted is He, when He addressed the bee with what has been mentioned, addressed the human and said: We inspired this bee with these marvels, so that there might emerge from their bellies a drink varying in its colours.

The second discussion: we have mentioned that some people say that honey is an expression for particles of dew that arise in the air and fall

Page 59

upon the tips of trees and upon the leaves and flowers, and the wasp picks them up with its mouth. If we take this view, then what is meant by His saying: ﴿There emerges from their bellies﴾ is: from their mouths, and every cavity inside the body is called a belly ("baṭn"). Do you not see that they say: "the bellies of the brain" (buṭūn al-dimāgh), meaning its cavities? So likewise here: there emerges from their bellies, that is, from their mouths. As for the view of the literalists, namely that the bee eats the leaves and fruits and then vomits, and that this is honey, the statement is clear.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿a drink, varying in its colours, in which is healing for mankind﴾. Know that He, exalted is He, described honey by these three attributes:

The first attribute: that it is a drink, and the matter is so, for it is sometimes drunk alone and sometimes made into beverages.

The second attribute: His saying: ﴿varying in its colours﴾, meaning: that among it is red, white and yellow. A parallel to this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And among the mountains are streaks, white and red, varying in their colours, and deep black﴾ [Fatir: 27]. The purpose of it is to refute the claim of nature, for this substance, though of uniform nature, came into being in varying colours, which shows that the occurrence of those colours is by the arrangement of a choosing agent, not for the sake of the creation of nature.

The third attribute: His saying: ﴿in which is healing for mankind﴾, and concerning it there are two views:

The first view, which is the correct one, is that it is an attribute of honey.

If they say: how can it be healing for people when it harms in cases of yellow bile and aggravates bitterness?

We say: He, exalted is He, did not say that it is a healing for all people, for every disease and in every condition. Rather, since it is a healing for some people with some ailments, it is fitting to describe it as having healing in it. What shows that it is a healing in general is that hardly any electuary (ma'jūn) is made whose completion and perfection is not achieved by kneading with honey, and also the beverages made from it are very beneficial in phlegmatic diseases.

The second view, which is the view of Mujahid, is that what is meant is: the Qur'an is a healing for mankind. On this interpretation, the account of the production of honey from the bee ends at His saying: ﴿There emerges from their bellies a drink varying in its colours﴾; then He begins and says: ﴿in it is healing for mankind﴾, meaning: in this Qur'an there has come about what is a healing for mankind from disbelief and innovation, like that which is in the story of the bee. It is reported from Ibn Mas'ud that honey is a healing from every disease, and the Qur'an is a healing for what is in the breasts.

Know that this view is weak, and two things indicate it:

The first: the pronoun in His saying: ﴿in it is healing for mankind﴾ must refer to the nearest of what has been mentioned, and that is nothing other than His saying: ﴿a drink varying in its colours﴾. As for ruling that this pronoun refers to the Qur'an, although it has not been mentioned previously, that is not appropriate.

The second: what Abu Sa'id al-Khudri narrated: that a man came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "My brother complains of his stomach." He said: "Give him honey to drink." He went and then returned and said: "I gave him to drink, but it did not avail him anything." He, peace be upon him, said: "Go and give him honey to drink." He went and gave him to drink, and it was as if he had been released from a shackle. He said: "Allah has spoken the truth and your brother's belly has lied." They understood His saying: "Allah has spoken the truth and your brother's belly has lied" as referring to His saying: ﴿in it is healing for mankind﴾, and that is only valid if this is an attribute of honey.

If someone says: what is meant by his saying, peace be upon him: "Allah has spoken the truth and your brother's belly has lied"?

Page 60

We say: perhaps he, peace be upon him, knew through the light of revelation that the benefit of that honey would appear later. Since its benefit did not appear at the time, although he, peace be upon him, knew that it would appear later, this was like a lie, and for this reason the term was applied to it.

Then God concluded the verse with His saying: ﴿Indeed in that is a sign for a people who give thought.﴾ Know that the explanation of this verse is from several aspects:

The first: the bee's specialization in those subtle sciences and obscure knowledge, such as building hexagonal hives and the other conditions we have mentioned.

The second: its guidance to all those honey-producing parts from the tips of trees and leaves.

The third: God's creation of the beneficial particles in the atmosphere of the air, then their being cast onto the tips of trees and leaves, then the inspiring of the bee to gather them after they have been scattered. All of this is wondrous, indicating that the God of the world built its arrangement upon regard for wisdom and benefit. And God knows best.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 16, verse 70 (part 1 of 2):

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And Allah created you, then He causes you to die; and among you is he who is returned to the most decrepit age, so that he knows nothing after knowing. Indeed Allah is Knowing, Competent.﴾

In the verse there are several issues.

The first issue: When He, exalted is He, mentioned some of the wonders of the states of animals, He then mentioned some of the wonders of the states of people. Among them is what is mentioned in this verse, which is an indication of the stages of human life. The wise (al-'Uqala') have arranged them into four stages:

The first of them: the age of growth and increase (sinn al-nashw wa'l-nama').
The second: the age of standing still, which is the age of youth (sinn al-shabab).
The third: the age of slight decline, which is the age of middle age (sinn al-kuhula).
The fourth: the age of great decline, which is the age of old age (sinn al-shaykhukha).

So He, exalted is He, argued from the transition of the living being from some of these stages to others, that this transferring agent is Allah, exalted is He. The physicians and naturalists (al-tabi'iyyun) said: the factor that necessitates this transition is the nature of the human being. I will relate their words in summarized form and show their weakness and corruption. At that point it remains that this transferring agent is Allah, glorified is He, and at that point what Allah, exalted is He, mentioned in this verse is established by rational proof. The naturalists said: The body of the human being is created from semen and menstrual blood, and semen and blood are two hot, moist substances. Heat, when it acts upon a moist body, reduces its moisture and gives it a kind of dryness, and this is observed and known. They said: So what is in these two substances of the power of heat continues to reduce what is in them of moisture, until the organs become firm, coagulation appears in it, and the bone, cartilage, nerve, sinew, ligament and the rest of the organs come into being. When the body is complete and perfected, at that time the fetus is separated from the mother's womb. Yet despite this the moistures are still excessive, and the proof of this is that you see the organs of the child after its separation from the mother soft and delicate, and its bones soft, close in nature to cartilage. Then the heat in the body acts upon those moistures and reduces them. They said: And the body undergoes three states.

The first state: that the moisture of the body is excessive over its heat, and at that time the organs are receptive to expansion, increase and growth, and that is the age of growth and increase, and its end is at thirty years or thirty-five years.

The second state: that the moistures of the body become less than they were, so that they suffice for preserving the innate original heat, but they are not excessive beyond this measure. This is the age of standing still and the age of youth, and its limit is five years, and at its completion the forty years are completed.

The third state: that the moistures decrease and become such that they no longer suffice for preserving the innate heat, and at that time decline appears. Then this decline may be hidden, and that is the age of middle age, and its completion is at sixty years; and it may be apparent, and that is the age of old age, and its completion is at one hundred and twenty years. This is what the physicians have obtained in this matter. In my view this explanation is weak, and several points show its weakness:

The first point: We say that at the beginning, when the semen was semen and the blood was blood, the moistures were predominant, the innate heat was submerged, and it was weak for this reason. Then, despite its weakness, it became strong enough to dissolve most of those moistures and separate them from the state of blood and semen until they became bone, cartilage, nerve and ligament. When the organs were formed and the body was complete, the moistures decreased, so it was necessary that the innate heat should have greater strength than it had before. Therefore it was necessary that the dissolution of the moistures after the formation and completion of the body should be greater than their dissolution before the formation of the body. It is known that the matter is not so, because before the formation of the body the substance of semen and blood underwent a transformation until it became bone and nerve, whereas after the formation of the body no such transformation occurred, nor even a tenth of a tenth of it. So if the formation of these organs were due to the effect of heat on moisture, it would necessarily follow that the dissolution of moistures after the completion of the body would be greater than their dissolution before the formation of the body. Since the matter is not so, we know that the formation of the body was by the arrangement of a powerful, wise Agent who orders the bodies of animals according to their benefits, and that the formation of the body was not for the reason they stated of the effect of heat upon moisture.

The second point in refuting this speech is that we say: the innate heat present in the body of the complete human being is either the very same that was present in the substance of the drop of semen, or it has become greater than it was. The first is false, because the innate heat present in the substance of the drop was proportionate to the bulk of the drop, and there is no doubt that the bulk of the drop was small and tiny. So this body, after its growth, if only that amount of innate heat had been present in it, would have been extremely little, and no effect from this body would have appeared at all.

As for the second, it concedes that the innate heat increases according to the increase of the mass and body. And if the innate heat increases moment by moment, and it is established that its increase necessitates the increase of strength and health moment by moment, then it would necessarily follow that the animal body remains forever in increase and perfection. Since the matter is not so, we know that the increase and decrease of the state of the animal body is not according to nature, but by the arrangement of a free agent.

The third point, which we raised against the physicians in our book "al-Kabir fi al-Tibb" (The Great Book on Medicine), we said: The innate moisture has become equal to the innate heat. Why do you say that the innate heat must become less than it was, and that the human being must pass from the age of youth to the age of decline? They said: The reason for this is that when this equilibrium arises, then the innate heat afterwards affects the lightening of the innate moisture, so the innate moistures decrease until they become such that they no longer suffice for preserving the innate heat. When this state occurs, the innate heat also weakens, because the innate moisture is like nourishment for the innate heat, so when the nourishment decreases, the one nourished weakens.

The summary is: the innate heat causes the scarcity of the innate moisture, and its scarcity causes the weakness of the innate heat, and the weakness of one of them necessitates the weakness of the other until it reaches the point where no innate moisture remains, and then the innate heat is extinguished and death occurs. This is the extent of what they said in this matter, and it is weak. For we say: If the innate heat affects the drying and reduction of the innate moisture, why is it not possible to say that the nutritive faculty supplies its replacement? At this point they said: The nutritive faculty can supply its replacement only if the innate heat is strong; but when it is weak, it cannot. We say: Here a circularity (dawr) arises, because the innate moisture decreases and falls only if the nutritive faculty is not sufficient to supply its replacement, and the nutritive faculty becomes unable to supply this only when the innate heat is weak, and the innate heat becomes weak only if the innate moisture decreases. Thus it is established that the doctrine they stated entails circularity, and that it is false. So it is established that explaining the transition of the human being from one age to another by what they mentioned, through considering the natures, necessitates these aforementioned difficulties for them, so saying so is false. And since this doctrine is false, it is necessary to affirm with certainty that these states are attributed to the God, the Powerful, Free-Choosing, Wise, Merciful, who orders the bodies of animals in the manner that accords with their benefits, and that is what was sought.

One day I was reading the Surah al-Mursalat, and when I reached His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Did We not create you from a worthless fluid? Then We placed it in a firm lodging for a known period. Then We determined, and excellent are We at determining. Woe that Day to the deniers.﴾ [al-Mursalat: 20–24], I said: There is no doubt that by "these deniers" are meant those who attributed the formation of animal bodies to natures and to the effect of heat upon moisture. And I believe from the core of my heart, O Lord of Might, that these arrangements are not from natures, but from the Creator of the world, who is the most wise of judges and the most generous of the generous.

Having known this, the truthfulness of His saying ﴿And Allah created you﴾ has been established by rational proof, because it is established that the creator of the bodies of people and of all animals is not nature, but Allah, glorified and exalted is He. As for His saying ﴿then He causes you to die﴾, we have shown that the cause they mentioned for the occurrence of death is corrupt and false, and that it necessitates the doctrine of circularity; and since that is invalid, it is established that life and death occurred only by the creation and decree of Allah. As for His saying ﴿and among you is he who is returned to the most decrepit age﴾, we have shown by proof that natures cannot be the cause of the human being's transition from perfection to deficiency and from strength to weakness, so it is necessary to affirm with certainty that the transition of the human being from youth to old age, from health to senility, and from complete intellect until he becomes senile and heedless, is not by the requirement of nature, but by the act of a free agent. When what we have mentioned is established, it becomes clear that what the wording of the Qur'an indicates has been confirmed in its soundness by the decisive text of the Qur'an.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed Allah is Knowing, Competent.﴾ This is like the foundation upon which all that we have mentioned is based, because nature is ignorant and cannot distinguish between the time of benefit and the time of harm, so these affections in this human being cannot be attributed to it. As for the God of the world, its Arranger and its Creator, He is perfect in knowledge and perfect in power; by the perfection of His knowledge He knows the measures of benefits and harms, and by the perfection of His power He is able to bring about benefits and repel harms. Therefore it is indeed possible to attribute the creation of animals to the God of the world, and it cannot be attributed to natures. And Allah knows best.

The second issue: On the interpretation of the words of the verse. The exegetes said: ﴿And Allah created you﴾ when you were not anything; ﴿then He causes you to die﴾ at the end of your appointed terms; ﴿and among you is he who is returned to the most decrepit age﴾, which is its worst and weakest. It is said: "razula al-shay' yarzulu razalah" and "arzalahu ghayruhu" (it became base, and another made it base). From it is His saying: ﴿except those who are our lowest ones﴾ [Hud: 27], and from it His saying: ﴿and the lowest ones have followed you﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 111]. As for His saying ﴿and among you is he who is returned﴾
[page 63] ﴿to the most decrepit age﴾, does it include the Muslim, or is it specific to the disbeliever? There are two opinions on this:

The first opinion: that it includes him. It has been said: it is the long life. On this interpretation it is reported from 'Ali, peace be upon him, that he said: the most decrepit age is seventy-five years. Qatada said: ninety years. As-Suddi said: it is senility (al-kharaf). The first opinion is preferable, because kharaf means the loss of intellect, and His saying ﴿and among you is he who is returned to the most decrepit age, so that he knows nothing after knowing﴾ indicates that He, exalted is He, returned him to the most decrepit age only in order to remove his intellect. So if the meaning of the most decrepit age were the loss of intellect, the thing would become the very purpose sought from it, and that is false.

The second opinion: this does not apply to the believers. The believer's age, when prolonged, only increases him in honour with God Most High, and it is not permissible to say of him that he is returned to the lowest age. The proof for this is the saying of God Most High: ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾ ﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ [al-Tin: 5-6]. So God Most High made clear that those who believed and did righteous deeds were not returned to the lowest of the low. 'Ikrimah said: Whoever recites the Qur'an will not be returned to the lowest age.

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing﴾, Ibn 'Abbas said: He means by what His friends and His enemies do, "Capable" of whatever He wills.

* * *

The third issue: just as this verse indicates the existence of the God, the Creator of the world who chooses freely, it also indicates the validity of resurrection and the Last Day. This is because man was pure non-existence, and God brought him into existence, then caused him to cease to exist a second time. This shows that since he was non-existent the first time, and his return to non-existence the second time was possible, likewise once he came into existence and then ceased, it must be possible for him to return to existence the second time. Also, he was dead when he was a drop of semen, then he became alive, then he died. Since the first death was possible, the return of death was possible; likewise, since the first life was possible, it must be possible for life to return a second time. Also, man in the first stage of his childhood is ignorant and knows nothing; then he becomes knowing, intelligent and understanding. Then when he reaches the lowest age, he returns to what he was in childhood, namely the lack of intellect and understanding. So the lack of intellect and understanding of the first time returns in exactly the same form at the end of his life. Likewise, the intellect that was acquired and then removed must be capable of returning a second time. When this whole argument is established, it is established that the one who died and ceased to exist may have his existence return, his life return, and his intellect return once more. And when the matter is so, it is established that the doctrine of resurrection, gathering and raising is true. And God knows best.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 16, verse 71:

His words, exalted is He: ﴿And Allah has favoured some of you over others in provision. Yet those who have been favoured do not give their provision to those whom their right hands possess, so that they are equal in it. Then is it the favour of Allah that they deny?﴾

Know that this is a consideration of another state of human beings. We see that the most astute and most intelligent of people spend their lives seeking a small measure of this world and it is not made easy for them, while we see the most ignorant and least intelligent of creatures having the doors of this world opened to them, and whatever occurs to their minds and passes through their imagination is immediately obtained for them. If the cause were human effort and intellect, the more intelligent would necessarily be more favoured in these states. Since we see that the more intelligent have a smaller share and the most ignorant and base have the greater share, we know that this is due to the division of the Divider, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Is it they who distribute the mercy of your Lord? We have distributed among them their livelihood in the life of this world﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 32].

And al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said:

"Among the evidence for destiny and its being is the misery of the intelligent and the good living of the fool."

Know that this disparity is not restricted to wealth, but is found in quickness and dullness, beauty and ugliness, intellect and foolishness, health and sickness, a good name and a bad name. This is a sea without a shore. I once accompanied some kings on some journeys, and that king had much wealth and standing, and many fine mounts were led before him, yet he could not ride any one of them; and often delicious foods and fragrant fruits were brought to him, yet he could not partake of any of them. Meanwhile, each of us was sound in temperament, strong in constitution, and in full vigour, yet he could not find his belly filled with food. So that king, although he surpassed this poor man in wealth, this poor man surpassed that king in health and strength. This is a broad subject, and when a person considers it, his wonder at it becomes great.

As for His words: ﴿so those who have been favoured do not give their provision to those whom their right hands possess﴾, there are two opinions:

The first opinion: The purpose of this statement is to affirm what preceded in the previous verse, that happiness and misfortune occur only from Allah, exalted is He. The meaning is: I am the provider of all of them, masters and slaves alike, so they are equal in My provision. Let the masters not suppose that they give their slaves any provision from themselves; rather, I have sent My provision to them through their hands. The summary of this view is that the intended purpose is to show that the Provider is Allah, exalted is He, and that the owner does not provide for the slave; rather, the Provider of both the slave and the master is Allah, exalted is He. The verification of the matter is that the slave may at times be more complete in intellect, stronger in body, and more aware of benefits and harms than the master, and this shows that the humiliation of that slave and the honour of that master are from Allah, exalted is He, as He said: ﴿You honour whom You will and You humble whom You will﴾ [Al 'Imran: 26].

The second opinion: The purpose of this verse is a refutation of those who ascribe partners to Allah, exalted is He. According to this opinion there are two aspects:

The first: that this is a refutation of the worshippers of idols and images, as if it were said: He, exalted is He, has favoured masters over their slaves, and has made the slave unable to possess anything alongside his master. Since you do not make your slaves equal to you in ownership, how can you make these lifeless things equal to Me in worship?

The second: Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, said: this verse was revealed concerning the Christians of Najran when they said: Jesus, son of Mary, is the son of Allah. The meaning is: you do not make your slaves partners with you in what you own so that they would be equal, so how do you make My servant a son to Me and a partner in divinity?

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿so that they are equal in it﴾. The meaning of the fa' in His words "fahum" is "until" (hatta). The meaning is: those who have been favoured do not give their provision to their slaves, until their slaves would be equal with them in ownership of it.

Then He said: ﴿Then is it the favour of Allah that they deny?﴾ Concerning this there are two issues:

The first issue: 'Asim, in the narration of Abu Bakr, read "tajhadun" with the ta' as address, in reference to His words "khalaqakum" and "faddala ba'dakum"; the rest read it with the ya' in reference to His words "fahum fihi sawa'". Abu 'Ubayda and Abu Hatim preferred this, because the report is closer to it, and also because the apparent address is to the Muslims, and the Muslims are not addressed with denying the favour of Allah, exalted is He.

The second issue: There is no doubt that the intended meaning of His words "Then is it the favour of Allah that they deny?" is a rebuke against the polytheists to whom Allah, exalted is He, directed this argument.

If it is asked: how do they become deniers of Allah's favour upon them through the worship of idols?

We say: there are two aspects to this:

The first aspect: since the giver of all good is Allah, exalted is He, whoever ascribes a partner to Allah has attributed some of those goods to other than Him, and so he is a denier that they come from Allah, exalted is He. Also, the people of natures and the people of the stars attribute most of these favours to natures and to stars, and this makes them deniers that they come from Allah, exalted is He.

The second aspect: al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is that when He, exalted is He, established these proofs, explained them, and made them manifest in such a way that every intelligent person understands them, this was a great bounty from Him upon creation. At this point He said: "Then is it the favour of Allah" in His establishing these clarifications and making these evident proofs clear "that they deny?"

The third issue: The "ba'" in His words "Then is it the favour of Allah" may be superfluous, because the verb "jahada" is not transitive with "ba'", just as you say: "khudh al-khitam" and "bi al-khitam" (take the halter), and "ta'allaqtu Zaydan" and "bi Zayd" (I clung to Zayd). It is also possible that juhud is intended as kufr (disbelief), and so it takes the "ba'" because it carries the meaning of kufr. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 16, verse 72:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And Allah has made for you spouses from among yourselves, and has made for you, from your spouses, sons and grandchildren (ḥafadah), and has provided for you good things. Do they then believe in falsehood and deny the blessing of Allah?﴾

Know that this is another kind of human condition, which Allah mentions in order to derive evidence from it for the existence of the Chooser, the Wise God. It also serves as a reminder of Allah's favour upon His servants through such blessings. As for His saying ﴿He has made for you spouses from among yourselves﴾, some have said that it means Allah created Hawwa' (Eve) from Adam's rib. This is weak, because His saying ﴿He has made for you spouses from among yourselves﴾ is addressed to everyone, so restricting it to Adam and Hawwa' contradicts the evidence. Rather, this ruling is general to all males and females. The meaning is that Allah created women so that men may marry them. The meaning of ﴿from among yourselves﴾ is like His saying ﴿then kill yourselves﴾ [al-Baqarah: 54], and His saying ﴿and greet one another﴾ [al-Nur: 61], meaning some of you upon others. A parallel to this verse is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And among His signs is that He created for you spouses from among yourselves﴾ [al-Rum: 21].

The physicians and the natural philosophers (ahl al-tabi'ah) said: the difference between male and female arises because whoever has a hotter temperament (mizaj) is male, and whoever has a greater coldness and moisture is female. They then said: if the semen flows to the right testicle of the male, and from it then flows to the right side of the womb, the child is a complete male in maleness. If it flows to the left testicle of the man, and from it then flows to the left side of the womb, the child is a complete female in femaleness. If it flows to the right testicle and from it then flows to the left side of the womb, the child is male in the nature of females. If it flows to the left testicle of the man and from it then flows to the right side of the womb, this child is female in the nature of males.

Know that the essence of this discussion is: maleness has as its cause heat and dryness, and femaleness has as its cause coldness and moisture. But this cause is extremely weak, for we have seen among women those whose temperament is extremely hot, and among men those whose temperament is extremely cold. Had the cause of maleness and femaleness been that, this would have been impossible. Thus it is established that the Creator of the male and the female is the eternal, Wise God. And by the evidence we have mentioned, the truth of His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿And Allah has made for you spouses from among yourselves﴾ has become manifest.

Then He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿and has made for you, from your spouses, sons and ḥafadah﴾. Al-Wahidi said: the root of ḥafadah is from ḥafad, which is lightness in service and work. It is said: ḥafada yaḥfidu ḥafadan and ḥufudan and ḥafadanan, meaning he hastened. From it comes the phrase in the supplication of qunut (the prayer supplication recited in the prayer): "And to You we hasten and serve (naḥfid)." The ḥafadah is the plural of al-ḥafid, and al-ḥafid is everyone who is light and swift in serving You and hastens in obedience to You. Its plural is said to be ḥafad without the taʾ, just as al-rasad is said. So the meaning of ḥafadah in the language is helpers and servants. Then it must be that what is meant by ḥafadah in this verse are the helpers who come to a man through his wife, because He said: ﴿and has made for you, from your spouses, sons and ḥafadah﴾. Therefore the helpers who do not come through the wife do not enter under this verse.

Having understood this, we say: it has been said that they are the in-laws of the wife's side (al-akhtan), and it has been said they are the relatives by marriage (al-aṣhar), and it has been said they are the children's children. The more preferable view is that all of these are included, because we have explained that the word admits all of them according to the shared meaning we mentioned.

Then He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿and has provided for you good things﴾. When He mentioned His favour upon His servants through spouses and what benefits and interests are in them, He mentioned His favour upon them through good foods, whether they come from plants, which are fruits, grains and drinks, or from animals.

Then He said: ﴿Do they then believe in falsehood?﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: meaning the idols. Muqatil said: meaning Satan. ʿAṭaʾ said: they affirm that I have a partner, a consort and a son. ﴿And they deny the blessing of Allah﴾, meaning by attributing these blessings to other than Allah and abandoning their attribution to Allah, may He be exalted.

There is another view concerning the verse: when He, may He be exalted, said ﴿and has provided for you good things﴾, He then said after it: ﴿Do they then believe in falsehood and deny the blessing of Allah?﴾ What is meant by this is that they prohibit for themselves good things which Allah has made lawful for them, such as the bahirah, the sa'ibah and the wasilah (pre-Islamic practices of designating certain animals as forbidden), and they permit for themselves forbidden things which Allah has prohibited for them, namely carrion, blood, the flesh of swine, and what is slaughtered on the nusub (stone altars). That is: why do they rule by those false judgments, and deny and reject Allah's favour in making good things lawful and bad things unlawful? And Allah knows best.

[p. 66]

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 16, verses 73–74:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they worship besides Allah that which possesses for them no provision from the heavens or the earth at all, and they are not able [to do so].﴾ ﴿So do not strike examples for Allah. Indeed, Allah knows, and you do not know.﴾

Know that when He, exalted is He, had explained many kinds of proofs for tawhid (the oneness of God), and just as these kinds are proofs for the soundness of tawhid, He likewise began by mentioning the categories of the noble and magnificent blessings. Then He followed this in this verse with a refutation of the idol-worshippers.

[Page 67]
So He said: ﴿And they worship besides Allah that which possesses for them no provision from the heavens or the earth at all, and they are not able [to do so].﴾ As for the provision that comes from the direction of the sky, it means the rain that comes from the sky, and as for that which comes from the direction of the earth, it is the plants and fruits that emerge from it. His saying, ﴿from the heavens and the earth﴾, the "min" is a qualifier of the indefinite noun which is His saying ﴿provision﴾, as if it were said: "They possess for them no provision from the rain and the plants." His saying ﴿at all﴾: al-Akhfash said: He made His saying ﴿at all﴾ a substitute (badal) for His saying ﴿provision﴾, and the meaning is: they possess no provision, neither little nor much. Then He said: ﴿and they are not able﴾. The benefit of this expression is that one who possesses nothing may still be described as being able to acquire it by some means, so Allah, exalted is He, made clear that these idols do not possess, and they also do not have the ability to obtain possession.

If it is said: He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And they worship besides Allah that which possesses﴾, so He referred to the idols with the form "ma" (that), which is used for non-rational beings, and then He said: ﴿and they are not able﴾. The plural with the "waw" and "nun" is specific to rational beings. How then can both be combined?

The answer: He referred to them with the word "ma" in consideration of what is the reality in fact, and He mentioned the plural with the "waw" and "nun" in consideration of what they believe about them, that they are gods.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿So do not strike examples for Allah﴾, and in this there are several aspects:

The first: The commentators said: it means, do not liken Him to His creation.

The second: Al-Zajjaj said: that is, do not make for Allah a likeness, because He is one with no like.

The third: I say it is possible that the intended meaning is that the idol-worshippers used to say: the God of the world is too exalted and too great for any one of us to worship Him directly; rather, we worship the stars, or we worship these idols, and the stars and idols are servants of the Greatest, Most Exalted God. The evidence for this is custom, for the lowly among people serve the great ones of the king's court, and those great ones serve the king; so it is likewise here. At this point Allah, exalted is He, said to them: Abandon the worship of these idols and stars, and do not strike the examples for Allah that you have mentioned, and be sincere in worshipping the Wise, the Powerful God.

Then He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah knows, and you do not know﴾, and in this there are two aspects:

The first: that Allah, exalted is He, knows the great punishment that is upon you because of worshipping these idols, and you do not know that; and if you knew it, you would abandon their worship.

The second: that Allah, exalted is He, when He forbade you from worshipping these idols, then abandon their worship, and abandon your argument upon which you relied, which is your saying: "Occupying oneself with worshipping the servants of the king is more fitting for honoring him than occupying oneself with worshipping the king himself." For this is an analogy (qiyas), and analogy must be abandoned when a text (nass) is present. Therefore He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah knows, and you do not know﴾.

[Page 68]

Then Allah, may He be exalted, says: ﴿Allah presents a parable: a slave owned, who has power over nothing; and one whom We have provided with goodly provision from Us, so that he spends from it secretly and openly. Are they equal? Praise belongs to Allah. But most of them do not know.﴾

Know that He, may He be exalted, confirmed the invalidity of the doctrine of the idol-worshippers through this example. There are several issues concerning it:

The first issue: regarding the interpretation of this parable, there are two opinions.

The first opinion: the meaning is that if we assume a slave owned, who has power over nothing, and we assume a free, noble, wealthy man who spends much, secretly and openly, then clear reason testifies that it is not permissible to equate the two in honour and reverence, just as it is not permissible to equate them in their common creation, form and humanity. How, then, may a rational person equate Allah, who is able to provide and bestow, with idols, which possess nothing and have no power whatsoever?

The second opinion: the "owned slave who has power over nothing" is the disbeliever. Since he has remained deprived of the worship of Allah, may He be exalted, and of His obedience, he has become like the humble, poor, powerless slave. The phrase ﴿and one whom We have provided with goodly provision from Us﴾ refers to the believer, for he is occupied with exalting the command of Allah, may He be exalted, and with compassion toward the creatures of Allah. Thus He, may He be exalted, made clear that the two are not equal in rank, nobility, or nearness to the good pleasure of Allah, may He be exalted.

Know that the first opinion is closer to the truth, because what precedes this verse and what follows it came to establish monotheism and to refute those who ascribe partners to Allah. Therefore, reading this verse according to this meaning is more appropriate.

The second issue: they differed regarding the intended meaning of His words ﴿a slave owned, who has power over nothing﴾. It was said: it refers to an idol, because it is a slave, as evidenced by His words: ﴿There is none in the heavens and the earth but that he comes to the Most Merciful as a slave﴾ [Maryam: 93]. As for it being owned and having power over nothing, this is evident. And His words ﴿and one whom We have provided with goodly provision from Us, so that he spends from it secretly and openly﴾ refer to the worshipper of the idol, because Allah, may He be exalted, provided him with wealth, and he spends from that wealth upon himself and upon his followers, secretly and openly.

Given this, we say: the two are not equal according to the immediate judgment of reason. Rather, clear reason testifies that the one who has power is more complete in state and more excellent in rank than that powerless one. Thus clear reason testifies here that the worshipper of an idol is more excellent than that idol. So how is it permissible to judge that the idol is equal to the Lord of the worlds in worship?

The second opinion: the intended meaning of His words ﴿a slave owned﴾ is a specific slave. It was said: he was a slave of Uthman ibn Affan, and they applied His words ﴿and one whom We have provided with goodly provision from Us﴾ specifically to Uthman.

The third opinion: it is general, applying to every slave with this attribute and to every free person with this attribute. This opinion is the most apparent, because it agrees with what Allah, may He be exalted, intended in this verse. And Allah knows best.

The third issue: the jurists (fuqaha) have used this verse as evidence that a slave does not own anything.

If they say: the apparent meaning of the verse indicates that a particular slave among the slaves has no power over anything; so why do you say that every slave is like this? We say: what indicates this are two aspects:

The first: it has been established in the principles of jurisprudence (Usul al-Fiqh) that a ruling mentioned immediately after a suitable attribute indicates that this attribute is the effective cause ('illah) of that ruling. Being a slave is an attribute that implies humiliation and subjugation, and His words ﴿has power over nothing﴾ is a ruling mentioned immediately after it. This implies that the cause of lacking power over anything is being a slave. By this method, generality is established.

The second: after it He, may He be exalted, said ﴿and one whom We have provided with goodly provision from Us﴾, thereby distinguishing this second category from the first category, the slave, by this attribute, namely that He provides him with provision. Therefore this attribute must not be attributed to the slave until the distinction between the second category and the first category is achieved. Had the slave owned, Allah would have given him goodly provision, because lawful ownership is goodly provision, whether it is little or much. Thus by these two aspects it is established that the apparent meaning of the verse implies that the slave has no power over anything and does not own anything.

[Page 69]

Then they differed. It is related from Ibn Abbas and others a strictness in this matter, to the point that he said: he does not even own divorce. Most of the jurists said: he does own divorce; he only does not own property or what is connected to property. They differed regarding whether, if the owner makes him own something, he owns it or not; and the apparent meaning of the verse negates this.

* * *

Questions remain concerning the verse:

The first question: why did He say ﴿owned, who has power over nothing﴾, when every slave is owned and unable to dispose of anything?

We say: as for mentioning "owned," it is so that the distinction between him and the free person is achieved, because a free person may be called a slave of Allah. As for His words ﴿has power over nothing﴾, the distinction may be achieved between him and the mukatab (a slave contracted to purchase his freedom) and the ma'dhun (a slave licensed to trade), because these two do not have power to dispose of things.

The second question: what is "man" (مَن) in His words ﴿and one whom We have provided﴾?

We say: the apparent view is that it is descriptive (mawsufah), as if it were said: "and a free man whom We provided," so that it corresponds to "a slave." It is not impossible that it be relative (mawsulah).

The third question: why did He say ﴿they are equal﴾ in the plural form?

We say: its meaning is "are free persons and slaves equal?" Then He said ﴿Praise belongs to Allah﴾, and in this there are several aspects:

The first: Ibn Abbas said: "Praise belongs to Allah for what He did with His friends and bestowed upon them with monotheism."

The second: the meaning is that all praise belongs to Allah, and none of the praise belongs to idols, because they have no blessing upon anyone.

His words ﴿But most of them do not know﴾ mean: they do not know that all praise belongs to Allah, and that none of it belongs to idols.

The third: al-Qadi said in the commentary: He said to the Messenger, peace be upon him, "Say: ﴿Praise belongs to Allah﴾." It is also possible that it is addressed to the one whom Allah provided with goodly provision, that he should say: "Praise belongs to Allah, who distinguished him in this capacity from that weak slave."

The fourth: it is possible that the meaning is that when He mentioned this parable, and it was a parable that matched the purpose and revealed the intended meaning, He said after it: ﴿Praise belongs to Allah﴾, meaning: praise belongs to Allah for the strength of this proof and the clarity of this evidence. Then He said: ﴿But most of them do not know﴾, meaning: despite its extreme clarity and utmost evidentness, these misguided people do not know it nor understand it.

**Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 16, verse 76:**

God, exalted is He, says: ﴿God strikes a parable: two men, one of them mute, unable to do anything, a burden upon his master; wherever he directs him, he brings no good. Are they equal, he and one who commands justice and is on a straight path?﴾

Know that God, exalted is He, refuted the claim of the worshippers of idols and images by this second parable. Its explanation is this: just as it is established in primary reason that a mute, incapable man is not equal in excellence and nobility to a speaking, capable, complete man, even though both share humanity, so it is more fitting to judge that inanimate matter is not equal to the Lord of the worlds in deserving worship. Then we say: there are two issues concerning the verse.

The first issue: God, exalted is He, described the first man with several attributes.

Page 70

The first attribute is "mute" (abkam). Regarding its interpretation there are several opinions, which al-Wahidi transmitted:

The first: Abu Zayd said: "A man who is abkam is one who is ʿayyi (inarticulate) and muqhamm (dull-tongued). He became mute (bakim) with bakam and bakamah." He also said: "The abkam is the one whose tongue is cut off, who does not speak well."

The second: Tha'lab related from Ibn al-A'rabi: "The abkam is the one who does not understand."

The third: al-Zajjaj said: "The abkam is the completely mute, who neither hears nor sees."

The second attribute is his saying: ﴿who is unable to do anything﴾, which indicates complete incapacity and total deficiency.

The third attribute is his saying: ﴿a burden upon his master﴾, meaning this mute, incapable man is a burden upon his master. The scholars of meanings (ahl al-maʿani, the linguistic exegetes) said: its root is from kalal, which is the opposite of sharpness: it is said "the knife was kalla" when its edge became dull and would not cut; and "his tongue was kalla" when it became heavy and he could not speak; and "so-and-so was kalla in the matter" when it weighed heavily upon him so that he did not rise to it. So his saying ﴿a burden upon his master﴾ means: heavy and weighty upon his master.

The fourth attribute: ﴿wherever he directs him, he brings no good﴾, meaning: wherever he sends him. The meaning of tawjih (directing) is that you send your companion in a specific direction of the road. It is said: "I directed him to such-and-such a place, and he headed toward it." His saying ﴿he brings no good﴾ means: because he is incapable, he does not do well and does not understand. Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Are they equal, he﴾, meaning: this one described by these four attributes, ﴿and one who commands justice﴾.

Know that the one who commands justice must necessarily be described as capable of speech, otherwise he would not be a commander. He must be capable, because commanding indicates a rank of authority, and that is not attained except with capability. He must be knowing, so that he can distinguish between justice and injustice. Thus it is established that describing him as one who commands justice entails describing him as capable and knowing. His being a commander contradicts the first being mute; his being capable contradicts the description of the first as one who ﴿is unable to do anything﴾ and as ﴿a burden upon his master﴾; and his being knowing contradicts the description of the first as one who ﴿brings no good﴾.

Then He said: ﴿and he is upon a straight path﴾, meaning: his being just, free from injustice and futility.

Once this is established, we say: it is evident by the immediate judgment of reason that the first and the second are not equal, and likewise here. And God knows best.

The second issue: concerning the intended meaning of this parable there are opinions, as in the preceding parable:

The first opinion: Mujahid said: "All of this is a parable of the God of creation and what is worshipped besides Him of falsehood. As for the mute, it is a parable of the idol, because it does not speak at all; likewise it is not capable of anything; and also it is a burden upon its worshippers, because it does not spend on them while they spend on it. Also, whatever matter the idol is directed to, it brings no good. As for the one who commands justice, he is God, glorified and exalted."

The second opinion: the intended meaning of this mute man is a slave of Uthman ibn Affan. That slave used to dislike Islam and had no good in him, while his master, Uthman ibn Affan, used to command justice and was upon the upright religion and the straight path.

The third opinion: the intended meaning is every slave described by these blameworthy attributes, and every free man described by those praiseworthy attributes. This opinion is better than the first, because God's describing the two as "two men" prevents applying it to an idol; likewise [the description as] mute and as a burden, and [the description of] directing toward sources of benefit. Likewise, describing the other as ﴿upon a straight path﴾ prevents applying it to God, exalted is He. Moreover, the purpose is to liken one image to another in a matter, and that likeness is not complete except when one of the two images differs from the other.

Page 71

As for the second opinion, it is also weak, because the purpose is to show the distinction between two men described by the attributes mentioned, and that is not specific to one particular person. Rather, whenever the difference in the mentioned attributes occurs, the purpose is achieved. And God knows best.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 16, verses 77–79:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿To Allah belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth. And the matter of the Hour is but as the blink of an eye, or it is even nearer. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.﴾ ﴿And Allah brought you out from the wombs of your mothers, knowing nothing, and He made for you hearing and sight and hearts that you might give thanks.﴾ ﴿Have they not considered the birds subjected in the atmosphere of the sky? None holds them up except Allah. Indeed, in that are signs for a people who believe.﴾

Know that when He, exalted is He, mentioned in the first verse the parable of the disbelievers as the mute, incapable one, and the parable of Himself as the one who commands justice while he is upon a straight path, and it is known that it is impossible for one to be commanding justice and upon a straight path except if he is perfect in knowledge and power, He mentioned in this verse the demonstration of His being perfect in knowledge and power. As for the demonstration of perfection of knowledge, it is His saying: ﴿To Allah belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth.﴾ The meaning: Allah knows the unseen of the heavens and the earth. Also, His saying: ﴿To Allah belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth﴾ conveys restriction (ḥaṣr); its meaning is that knowledge of these unseen things belongs to none but Allah. As for the demonstration of perfection of power, it is His saying: ﴿And the matter of the Hour is but as the blink of an eye, or it is even nearer.﴾ The Hour (al-sāʿah) is the time in which the Resurrection occurs; it was named "sāʿah" because it comes upon a person in an hour, and creation dies with a single cry. His saying: ﴿as the blink of an eye﴾ — al-lamḥ (the glance) is looking quickly; it is said: he glanced at him with his sight, a glance (lamḥan) and a glimpse (lamaḥānan). The meaning: the matter of the Resurrection, in speed, is only like the glance of the eye, and the purpose of it is to establish perfection of power. His saying: ﴿or it is even nearer﴾ means: the blink of the eye is an expression for the movement of the body called the glance from the top of the pupil to its bottom. There is no doubt that the pupil is composed of parts that are not divisible, so the glance of the eye is an expression for passing over the totality of those parts of which the surface of the pupil is composed. There is no doubt that those parts are many, and the time in which the glance of the eye occurs is composed of successive instants, and Allah, exalted is He, is capable of establishing the Resurrection in one of those instants; therefore He said: ﴿or it is even nearer﴾. However, since the swiftest of states and events in our intellects and thoughts is the blink of the eye, it is certainly for this reason that He mentioned it. Then He said: ﴿or it is even nearer﴾, as an alert to what we have mentioned. There is no doubt that the intended meaning is not the manner of doubt; rather the intended meaning is: "nay, it is even nearer." Al-Zajjaj said: the intended meaning is ambiguity toward the addressees, that He, exalted is He, brings the Hour either in the measure of the blink of an eye or in something swifter.
